title.en: Hot Air Balloon Flight over Putrajaya

overview: Be treated aerial views over Putrajaya during a hot air balloon ride, departing in the morning. This scenic 45- to 60-minute flight offers an unforgettable sunrise and a sweeping vista of Putrajaya’s landmarks and lovely lake. Peer down at the Wawasan Bridge, Putra Mosque (Masjid Putra) and Palace of Justice, among a few. Breakfast plus hotel pickup and drop-off included.
highlights: Putrajaya hot air balloon ride
Soar for 45 minutes to 1 hour on a scenic flight
Receive breakfast and a post-flight certificate
Hotel pickup and drop-off included
expect: Add a hint of adventure to your travel itinerary in Malaysia, by booking a magical experience which starts with a spectacular view of the country’s administrative capital, Putrajaya. This favorite Malaysian capital is a gourmet paradise of beautiful, scenic landscapes as well as modern architectural buildings, with lots of different on-ground activities, suitable for everyone to enjoy.

Make your way to Putrajaya by arranging for a special pick-up service right from your hotel in Putrajaya; which will bring you straight to the launch site. At the launch site, there is nothing quite like watching the hot air balloon fire up in the early morning breeze, while you kick-start your morning with a refreshing cup of coffee and light pastries. Before flight, of course, you would be briefed by an experienced hot air balloon pilot on safety, as well as what to expect on a hot air balloon ride.

When the balloon is ready to go, climb aboard a sturdy basket, which holds a maximum of 6 people, and then you’re ready to experience the thrill as your balloon fires up in the morning air and you slowly begin to rise over the scenery. While you glide and soar gracefully in the beautiful sky for at least 45 minutes, the pilot will accompany you on the ride to ensure everyone’s safety and provide narration on passing scenery. You will have plenty of picture- perfect opportunities, so make sure your camera is ready.

After your 45-minute flight, you can participate in the packing up of the balloon, which at times, can be quite an adventure. You will then get to toast your celebratory flight with a glass of sparkling juice, have a hearty breakfast at the stunning Cyberview Resort and Spa Hotel and to top it off; you will receive a certificate of completion, which you can share with family and friends.

title.en: Kuala Selangor Tour from Kuala Lumpur with Fireflies Boat Ride and Seafood Dinner

overview: Get back to nature with a night away from Kuala Lumpur on a visit to Kuala Selangor. Tour a royal burial ground, an ancient fort and a local fishing village—where you’ll also enjoy a seafood dinner filled with fresh catch—and float through mangroves. Witness the wonder of thousands of glittering fireflies as the sun set and evening falls.
highlights: Kuala Selangor Tour from Kuala Lumpur
Marvel at the beautiful twinkling lights of the thousands of fireflies at night – a truly magical experience!
Explore a royal burial ground and Kota Melawati, an ancient fort
Enjoy a relaxing, scenic evening boat ride through the mangroves of Kuala Selangor
Dine on a fresh seafood dinner at a local fishing village
expect: Your friendly guide and professional driver will meet you at your hotel for this Kuala Selangor Tour from Kuala Lumpur with fireflies boat ride and seafood dinner. Travel by bus northeast of the city to Kuala Selangor. Once the royal capital of the state and home to Kampung Kuantan, this destination is home to one of the world’s largest firefly colonies. Upon arrival, make your way to Kota Melawati near the mouth of the Selangor River. Venture into the ruins of this ancient fort with your guide and learn about the cannons and other remnants from the 1900s. You’ll also tour the Royal Mausoleum where graves of the first three Sultans of Selangor are buried. Climb the 100 stairs to the top of Selangor Hill and learn about the much-storied execution block.

After that, head to Kuala Selangor Nature Park and gaze up at migratory birds. Keep your eyes peeled for silver-leaf monkeys, rare butterflies and indigenous birds. As the sun sets you’ll head to a nearby fishing village for a typical seafood dinner before making your way to Kampung Kuantan. Set sail on a Malaysian rowboat and take in the quiet beauty that surrounds you as your oarsman rows upstream through picturesque mangroves. Once darkness falls you’ll bear witness to thousands of sparkling fireflies. Your magical boat ride will last between 30 and 45 minutes. Upon completion you’ll head to shore and make your way back to your Kuala Lumpur hotel in the comfort of your air-conditioned vehicle.

title.en: Kuala Selangor Fireflies River Ride Including Dinner from Kuala Lumpur

overview: Take a riverboat ride to see the twinkling fireflies in the mangroves of Kuala Selangor. With a guide you'll visit Bukit Melawati and a Chinese fishing village, then indulge in a delicious seafood dinner served at a riverside restaurant. Finally, be amazed by the stars of Kampung Kuantan: bioluminescent fireflies (aka lightning bugs) that flash in synchronicity in the sky. Round-trip hotel transport is provided from Kuala Lumpur.
highlights: Kuala Selangor firefly show with dinner
Stop in Bukit Melawati to feed silvered leaf monkeys
Savor a seafood dinner at a riverside cafe
Take a riverboat ride to watch fireflies light up the night
Hotel pickup and drop-off included from Kuala Lumpur
expect: Your 8-hour tour begins with hotel pickup in Kuala Lumpur in the afternoon. En route to your destination in the district of Kuala Selangor, stop first in Bukit Melawati. Learn about the hill’s tumultuous past and get a close encounter with the silvered leaf monkeys that will climb onto your shoulder for food.

On arrival at the Selangor River, you’re served a seafood dinner at a restaurant on the riverbank. Savor the sunset while fishing boats glide past, then depart for Kampung Kuantan, known for its firefly colony.

During your boat ride, watch the firefly show and be charmed by these magnificent insects that shimmer with bioluminescence in the night sky. Afterward, you’re transported back to your hotel in Kuala Lumpur.

title.en: 7-Day Best of Malaysia: Cameron Highlands, Penang, Kota Bharu and Terengganu Tour Round-Trip from Kuala Lumpur

overview: Experience the best of Malaysia with this 7-day coach tour with round-trip travel from Kuala Lumpur. Make stops in five incredible destinations, including Cameron Highlands, Kota Bharu, and Kuantan. Discover the beauty, culture and history along with your informative local guide. Tour a tea plantation, climb 272 steps to the top of Sam Poh Tong cave temple, visit the Islamic Civilization Park and tour a tea plantation as part of this epic journey. Your tour also includes a stop at the picturesque Kuala Sepetang mangrove forest and a ride around the UNESCO World Heritage site of Georgetown in a traditional trishaw. Round-trip hotel transport is included and interested travelers can upgrade to include an optional airport transfer.
highlights: 7-day guided Malaysia highlights tour, round-trip by coach from Kuala Lumpur
Tour a scenic Cameron Highlands tea plantation and stop in the royal town of Kuala
Kangsar
See top attractions in Penang, including UNESCO-listed Georgetown and Fort
Cornwallis
Visit Kek Lok Si — the Pagoda of 10,000 Buddhas — and the cave temple of Sam
Poh Tong
Experience the wet market of Kota Bharu and the heritage waterfront city of Kuala
Terengganu
Marvel at replicas of famous world monuments at the Islamic Civilization Park, situated on Wan Man Island
Hotel pickup and drop-off included, with optional upgrades for airport transfers available on Days 6 or 7
expect: Experience the beauty of Malaysia’s coastal villages, cultural attractions, religious temples and historical landmarks on this seven-day Best of Malaysia Tour with stops in Cameron Highlands, Penang, Kota Bharu and Terengganu. This trip popular trip includes round-trip coach transportation from the capital city, as well as accommodation. Travelers can opt for a late evening flight (own expense) on day six from the Kuantan airport or return by coach to Kuala Lumpur on day seven. (Upgrades that include airport transfers are available.) Personalize your trip by choosing from single, twin or triple-accommodations with 3-, 4- and 5-star hotel options. Breakfast buffets included, as well as plenty of time to enjoy the amenities at each of the unique resorts.

Itinerary Day 1: Kuala Lumpur – Cameron Highlands Start with pickup from your hotel or meet your guide at Corus Hotel Kuala Lumpur, departing for the Cameron Highlands in the morning. You’ll drive a distance of 137 miles (220 km), stopping en route to see a local basket-weaving cottage industry, followed by a visit to Lata Iskandar Waterfall and a native settlement. Your knowledgeable guide accompanies your group to each location and offers interesting commentary on cultural and geographical features along the way.

Upon arrival at Cameron Highlands, one of Malaysia’s largest hill stations, you’ll be immersed in wondrous landscapes along the northeast side of the Pahang Mountains. Here, at an elevation of 5,060 feet (1,542 meters), the gentle slopes of the highlands offer cool temperatures and crisp air.

Your tour along this scenic plateau — well-known for its tea estates, farmland, rivers, lakes and orchards — includes a visit to a tea plantation, tea factory, market and butterfly farm. In the evening, sip tea on a large, private balcony as you relax and take in the views overlooking beautiful gardens. Your fine hill resort, situated on 7 acres (2.8 hectares), offers a mountain- rustic yet elegant atmosphere. Classic but contemporary rooms are furnished with teak furniture and have modern bathrooms with black granite flooring. Overnight: Strawberry Park Resort in the Cameron Highlands
Day 2: Cameron Highlands – Penang (B)

After a buffet breakfast, hop aboard the coach in the early morning. During the 205-mile (330-km) scenic drive to Penang, make a stop in Gunung Rapat to visit Sam Poh Tong, said to be the largest cave temple in Malaysia. As your guide accompanies you up the 246 steps to the top, hear about the legend of the 19th-century Chinese monk who discovered the cave. Your climb is rewarded with a scene of beautifully carved Buddha statues interspersed among the cavern’s stalactites and stalagmites.

Make a second coach stop in the royal town of Kuala Kangsar, where the impressive golden- domed exteriors of Ubudiah Mosque and Istana Iskandariah (the Royal Palace) provide unique photographic opportunities. After visiting the former royal residence of Istana Kenangan, which today houses the Royal Museum of Perak, continue on to the Kuala Sepetang mangrove forest.

Considered Malaysia’s best-managed mangrove forest, Kuala Sepetang serves an essential ecological role in protecting the coastline from erosion. Following a stroll along a boardwalk with your guide through the natural mangrove forest, you’ll visit a charcoal kiln where the bulk of the nation’s top-quality mangrove charcoal is produced. In the late afternoon, cross over into Penang via Penang Bridge. Spanning eight miles (13.5 km) across, it’s one of the longest bridges in the world.

Located on the northwest coast of Penang Island, your hotel makes use of a beachfront setting at the quieter end of the lovely Batu Ferringhi (Foreigner’s Rock) beach. The resort overlooks a tranquil and scenic bay, and each spacious room includes a private balcony. Enjoy entertainment and recreational amenities, including an outdoor swimming pool, tennis court, spa and fitness center. Overnight: Bayview Beach Resort in Penang
Day 3: Georgetown, Penang (B)

Leaving your hotel by coach after breakfast, drive to historical Georgetown, located just 25 minutes away. Upon arrival at the UNESCO World Heritage site, embark on a comprehensive sightseeing tour with your guide to see Georgetown’s top cultural attractions. View the third-longest reclining Buddha figure in the world, followed by a visit to Kek Lok Si Temple, also known as Pagoda of 10,000 Buddhas.Climb the steps to the temple and explore the area, which includes a magnificent bronze statue of Guanyin, the Goddess of Mercy, and a seven-story pagoda featuring 10,000 alabaster and bronze Buddha statues. Continue by coach to Fort Cornwallis, the landing site of Captain Francis Light when he arrived in 1786 to start the first British colony in Penang. Inside the fort walls there are original, century-old structures like the chapel, prison cells and munitions storage, as well as bronze cannons and flagstaffs belonging to the English East India Company. Then head to the waterfront village of the Weld Quay Clan Jetties, one of the last remaining old Chinese settlements on the island, where you’ll find houses built on stilts along the planks. Driving along Pitt Street, also known as the Street of Harmony, view the churches, Chinese temples, mosques and Hindu temples that have stood side by side for centuries in harmonious coexistence. Visit the intricate Khoo Kongsi clan house — part of a close-knit network of Chinese clan associations established in Malaysia in the mid-19th century. Finally, enjoy a breezy trishaw ride, still a popular mode of transport in Georgetown. Pass charming colonial buildings and modern skyscrapers before returning to your hotel to spend the rest of your day at your leisure. In the late evening, feel free to explore the nightlife along Batu Ferringhi. Overnight: Bayview Beach Resort in Penang
Day 4: Penang – Kota Bharu (B)

Following breakfast, depart Penang for Kota Bharu, a distance of approximately 250 miles (400 km). Journey east across Peninsular Malaysia through the main mountain range, which offers breathtaking views of the dense tropical rainforest while you travel through villages and plantations. En route to your destination, make a photo stop on Banding Island with its scenic lookout over the picturesque Temenggor Lake. Enjoy the calm lake surrounded by the immense rainforest — a perfect spot for a lunch break at a hotel restaurant with window views (own expense).

Farther, on, your coach stops at the highest mountain point along the route; located 3,445 feet (1,050 meters) above sea level, this overlook offers impressive vistas of the forested Titiwangsa mountain range as well as Thailand over the Malaysian border. On arrival in the state of Kelantan, proceed to the border town of Rantau Panjang, a popular meeting and trading point for the people of both countries. From the Malaysian side of the border, look for Thai villages across the Golok River — a lifeline for residents on both sides, as it provides the water supply for daily and agricultural use.

If you’d like, peruse a variety of products at the duty-free shops before settling in for the evening in Kota Bharu at your Marriott accommodation, the only 5-star international hotel in town. Choose from several dining options at the hotel’s restaurants or lounge, enjoy the pool or fitness center, or head to the spa for ultimate relaxation. Overnight: Renaissance Kota Bharu in Kota Bharu
Day 5: Kota Bharu – Kuala Terengganu (B)

Start your day with breakfast, followed by a visit to the colorful wet market of Kota Bharu and the area’s traditional cottage industries, such as silver handicrafts and songket weaving. Then reboard the coach for a 105-mile (170-km) drive south along the scenic coastline toward the heritage waterfront city of Kuala Terengganu. Taste some keropok, the popular local chips made of fish or prawns, before checking in to your hotel. The remainder of the day is yours to spend at your leisure. Overnight: Felda Residence Kuala Terengganu
Day 6: Kuala Terengganu – Kuantan (B)

Check out of your hotel after an early breakfast to embark on a 155-mile (250-km) journey by coach toward your next destination, Kuantan. First, stop en route to visit Pulau Duyong (Duyong Island), famous in the region for its traditional boat making. Accessible via a bridge, the island village involves a bit of walking with your guide, who shares interesting facts about the boats’ construction — they’re created without metal nails — as you watch a master boatman at work.

The Islamic Civilization Park, situated on Wan Man Island, is another must-see local attraction. The theme park showcases 20 replicas of the world’s great Islamic monuments, such as Spain’s Alhambra citadel, the Taj Mahal of India, the Masjid-al Haram of Saudi Arabia, Jerusalem’s Dome of the Rock and many more. Your guide ensures that you visit the iconic Grand Crystal Mosque, the highlight of the park.

Continue with a visit to a brassware-making center before heading farther south toward Cherating in the district of Kuantan. Your coach stops at a scenic coastal fishing village where you tour a sea turtle information center to learn more about these endangered species. En route, taste lemang, rice cooked with coconut milk in bamboo — a popular Malay specialty not to be missed — followed by afternoon tea hosted by the local community. Cherating’s main attractions include a village resident’s entertaining monkey that is trained to pluck coconuts from a tree, and a visit to a local cottage industry, where you can see mengkuang leaves being weaved into bags and mats.

After this bit of sightseeing, you can relax at your world-class beach resort, located on the pristine shoreline of Balok Beach. Gaze at the cobalt waters of the South China Sea from your private balcony, stroll the lush green garden or retire under a coconut palm. Refresh in the outdoor free-form swimming pool and hot tub, or head to the Samsara Spa for a full range of treatments. You’ll find plenty of gourmet delights as you dine in elegant surroundings or head to the bar for a cocktail under a lush canopy of trees. (Spa, drinks and dining options are your own expense.) If you prefer not to stay overnight and travel overland back to Kuala Lumpur the next day, you may schedule a flight from Sultan Ahmad Shah Airport in Kuantan, departing anytime after 8:30pm. Airport drop-off is available with your upgrade. Overnight: Swiss Garden Resort and Spa in Kuantan Day 7: Kuantan – Kuala Lumpur (B) After breakfast, you’re driven back to Kuala Lumpur, a distance of 168 miles (270 km). Hotel drop-off is included, or upgrade to a transfer to Kuala Lumpur International Airport.

title.en: Historical Malacca Full-Day Tour from Kuala Lumpur including Lunch

overview: Visit historic Malacca City, the capital of the Malaysian state of Malacca, on this guided, full-day sightseeing tour from Kuala Lumpur. Visit some of the most popular top sites in this UNESCO World Heritage City, like the 16th-century, Portuguese St. Paul’s Church and A Famosa fortress, Christ Church, the Stadthuys in the Red Square and much more. Enjoy a traditional Malaysian lunch and explore Jonker Street, the center street of Chinatown. Hotel pickup and drop-off and any necessary entrance fees are included.
highlights: Day trip to Malacca from Kuala Lumpur
Walk up St Paul's Hill and visit the ruins of St Paul's Church
Get panoramic views of the Malacca Strait and Bandar Hilir
Savor a typical Nyonya lunch in a local restaurant
Stroll through antique row of Jonker Street and take in the bustling street market
Learn the history of this important colonial port from your knowledgeable guide
expect: After a Kuala Lumpur hotel pickup, travel approximately two hours south in a comfortable, air-conditioned motor coach for a full day of sightseeing in Malacca City on the Malay Peninsula's southwest coast.

Begin with a visit to the Stadthuys, a historical landmark structure located in the heart of Malacca City in the Red Square. Then take in a panoramic view of Malacca City and the surrounding region from the top of St. Paul’s Hill, which features historic St. Paul’s Church, the oldest church building in Malaysia and Southeast Asia and part of the Malacca Museum Complex.

Enjoy a traditional Malaysian lunch at a local eatery, then follow the guide to Jonker Street, the center street of Chinatown. Once renowned for its antique shops, Jonker Street now features clothing and craft outlets as well as restaurants.

Finally, visit the A Famosa fortress, which is among the oldest surviving European architectural remains in southeast Asia, and stop at Cheng Hoon Teng, a Chinese temple practicing the Three Doctrinal Systems of Taoism, Confucianism and Buddhism. The tour ends with a return trip to Kuala Lumpur.

overview: Get a taste of Malaysia’s finest foods on this guided, 3- to 4- hour, small-group walking and riding tour around Kuala Lumpur. Stop by three or more street vendors and hidden-gem restaurants off-the-beaten path to sample the best Malaysian cuisine. Learn about Malaysian customs and culture and visit food spots like mamak stalls and round- the-clock hawker centers (open-air food courts). All food tastings, including beverages, and any necessary transportation are included.
highlights: 3- to 4- hour food tour in Kuala Lumpur
Experience KL's lively food culture at one or two of its popular hawker centers
Sample street food from local food stalls and discover hidden gems with an expert guide
Learn about Malaysian customs as you meet friendly locals
Try Malaysian delicacies from at least three different vendors/restaurants – and feast on as much as you can eat!
Enjoy air-conditioned transport between all food stops
Small-group tour limited to 4 people ensures a personalized experience with your guide
expect: Meet the guide and the rest of the small group at the Taman Paramount Light Rail Transit (LRT) station in Petaling Jaya. One possibility would be the Bangsar area, boasting a wide variety of food spots like mamak stalls with traditional Tamil-Muslim cuisine, plus South Indian banana-leaf restaurants and Malay warungs, or small, family-owned restaurants offering both local and Western food. Also, visit some of the food stalls in a round-the-clock hawker center (an open-air food court) in Petaling Jaya, or head to Brickfields to see some of their South Indian restaurants and Chinese coffee shops serving traditional Chinese fare like dim sum. Allow the knowledgeable guide to make the selections of local favorites. Try dishes like nasi lemak (coconut rice with chili paste, anchovies, peanuts and vegetables; stir-fried Chinese noodles; Indian breads with chicken, fish and mutton curry; desserts like ondeh ondeh (rice balls with palm sugar and coconut shavings).

title.en: Batu Caves and Temple Tour from Kuala Lumpur

overview: Explore the culture and traditions of Malaysia on this three- hour Batu Caves and Temple tour from Kuala Lumpur. Spend the afternoon visiting these famed natural caverns with your expert local guide and wander the impressive grounds of the Batu Cave Hindu Temple, where you’ll gain insight and understanding of the religious roots of this incredible and diverse nation. Drive through Little India, learn about the art of batik and pewter smithing and enjoy round-trip transportation and hotel pick up and drop off.
highlights: Afternoon exploration of Batu Caves from Kuala Lumpur, led by a professional guide
Drive along Little India (Brickfields) and admire the colorful community of local shops and quaint restaurants
Be greeted by comical monkeys at the Batu Caves Hindu temple
Climb the 272 steps that lead you into the spectacular caverns
See the art of Batik silk designing and learn about pewter arts at the Royal Selangor
Visitor Center Hotel pickup and drop-off included
expect: Your cultural tour of Malaysia kicks off with hotel pick up. Meet your friendly local guide and professional driver in Kuala Lumpur and begin this memorable three-hour Batu Caves and Temple Tour. You’ll drive through Little India, a neighborhood in Brickfields known for it’s colorful streets, flavorful cuisine and unique shops.

The 30-minute scenic drive ends at the Batu Caves. These natural limestone masses are home to Hindu shrines that house various religious deities. Learn from your guide about the deep Hindu roots of this nation as you make your wau up the 272 steps to the golden Lord Murugan.
Once you arrive at the top, you’ll head to Cathedral Cave—the largest in the complex. Your guide will offer background on the significance of this space, which houses intricate Hindu shrines.

On your way back to Kuala Lumpur, stop at an area batik center and learn about this traditional art is made. You’ll also visit the Royal Selangod Visitor Center to learn about the ancient art of pewter smithing before returning to your hotel.

title.en: Private Tour: Half Day Batu Caves Tour

overview: Take a private tour of Batu Caves during a morning or afternoon excursion by private vehicle. Climb the 272 steps to the Hindu shrine dedicated to Lord Subramaniam and admire the limestone caves. Your driver-guide makes stops at the Malaysian Batik Cottage as well as the Royal Selangor Pewter Factory along the way. Hotel pickup and drop-off included from Kuala Lumpur.
highlights: Private tour of Batu Caves
Huff up the steep steps to the enshrined cave
Discover Hindu traditions and beliefs
Stop at the Royal Selangor Pewter Factory
Private hotel transport included
expect: Start your excursion with the visit of the Malaysian Batik Cottage as well as a short stop at the Royal Selangor Pewter factory. You will then proceed to the well-known Batu Caves, which has 272 steps to reach the shrine of the Hindu deity Lord Subramaniam and set within an outcrop of lime stone caves.

The main Hindu festivals are celebrated every year at Batu Cave including “Diwali” or Deepavali, that celebrate the victory of light over darkness; and also since 1892, the festival of Thaipusam, one of the biggest celebration for Hinduism community from all over the world. During Thaipusam, the procession of the event actually begins from a Temple ("Maha Mariamman" Temple, the oldest one in Kuala Lumpur built in 1873) located in the city center of Kuala Lumpur, barely a street behind the ever busy China Town. Batu cave remains the most interesting place outside of India to get a chance to observe and attend to the main celebrations of the Hindu community from India, Australia or Singapore. Hinduism remains a minority religion in Malaysia. An estimated 9% of the total population of Malaysia are ethnic Indians, of whom almost 89% are practicing Hinduism. Indian settlers came to Malaysia in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. Many of these came to work as laborers on rubber plantations, while those who were English-educated occupied more professional positions.
This visit is not only a great opportunity to discover more about Hinduism traditions and beliefs, It is also a unique way to learn about the history of Malaysia and understand its multiculturalism.

overview: Make the most of your layover in Kuala Lumpur with this private city sightseeing tour. Enjoy a full day of all the highlights, like Petronas Twin Towers, the Craft Cultural Complex and the National Museum. Enjoy the expertise of a private guide and the luxury of transport in a private vehicle. This tour includes the flexibility to plan your own itinerary based on time and interest and hotel or airport drop-off is included.
highlights: Full-day private layover tour in Kuala Lumpur
Visit top attractions in the city center with a private guide

expect: A long layover doesn’t have to mean wasted time thanks to this private Kuala Lumpur layover tour that includes city sightseeing and airport or hotel drop off. Enjoy the luxury of private transportation and a friendly local guide on a tour that’s personalized to meet your expectations, interests and time constraints.

You’ll stop at the Petronas Twin Towers—the world’s tallest, and one of Kuala Lumpur’s must-see landmarks. Take photographs of this 88-story building that’s constructed from some 55,000 glass panels and stainless steel beams.

Gain a deeper understanding and appreciation for local artisans on a visit to the Craft Cultural Complex, where handmade items from across the country are proudly displayed and available for purchase. Your guide will show you the impressive cultural exhibits and detail characteristics that help to distinguish works in one region from another. Meet resident artists and participate in hands-on experiences on this tour highlight. Next you’ll check out the Royal King’s Palace, known by locals as Istana Negara before making your way to the National Museum. This gem of a destination will unlock the history, wildlife and traditions of Malaysia and your guide will offer insight into the artifacts on display as you wander the galleries.

This tour will take you past the National Mosque and Railway Administration Building, as well as to Independence Square, where you’ll see the country’s first flag proudly displayed. Your private tour and memorable day ends with hotel or airport drop off, depending on your travel plans.

overview: This private full-day tour of historical Malacca from Kuala Lumpur was designed with history buffs in mind.

The flexibility and personalization of a private guide means you can explore Malaysia’s oldest trading port with convenience and ease. Gain a deeper understanding of how the Portuguese, Dutch and English influenced the state of Malacca as you explore the streets. Sample local cuisine and regional flavors with a traditional lunch before you return to Kuala Lumpur in your private, air-conditioned vehicle.
highlights: Explore colorful and old trading port of Malacca on this private full-day tour from
Kuala Lumpur
Your own English-speaking guide
Walk through the ruins of St. Paul's Church
Visit the oldest Chinese temple in Malaysia, Cheng Hoon Teng
Lunch at a local restaurant
Hotel pickup and drop off
expect: The colorful and historic port town of Malacca is located roughly two hours south of Kuala Lumpur. This private full-day tour of historical Malacca transports you from one of the nation’s biggest cities to its third smallest state for a whirlwind cultural experience Follow your expert local guide on a private tour through the trading ports that have existed through English, Dutch and Portuguese rule. Learn about the role this port played in commerce as your guide shares insight and history throughout the tour. You’ll visit St. Paul’s Hill, where panoramic views of the historic state and the old town of Bandar Hilir prove th perfect photo op. Get an up-close look at the Portuguese Fort de Santiago and the ruins of St. Paul’s Chuch, as well the Dutch tombstones that line the grounds.

Once you’ve taken in the sites, head to a local restaurant with your guide where you’ll enjoy a savory lunch (included) of regional specialties that blend Chinese and Malay flavors. Wander along Jonker Street and comb through some of the unique shops before making your way back to Kuala Lumpur. En route to your hotel, you’ll make a stop at the Cheng Hoon Teng temple—the oldest Chinese temple in the country. This unique destination offers incredible views of Kampong Kling, a nearby Malay village.

title.en: 7-Day Best of Malaysia: Cameron Highlands, Penang, Kota Bharu and Terengganu Tour Round-Trip from Kuala Lumpur

overview: Experience the best of Malaysia with this 7-day coach tour with round-trip travel from Kuala Lumpur. Make stops in five incredible destinations, including Cameron Highlands, Kota Bharu, and Kuantan. Discover the beauty, culture and history along with your informative local guide. Tour a tea plantation, climb 272 steps to the top of Sam Poh Tong cave temple, visit the Islamic Civilization Park and tour a tea plantation as part of this epic journey. Your tour also includes a stop at the picturesque Kuala Sepetang mangrove forest and a ride around the UNESCO World Heritage site of Georgetown in a traditional trishaw. Round-trip hotel transport is included and interested travelers can upgrade to include an optional airport transfer.
highlights: 7-day guided Malaysia highlights tour, round-trip by coach from Kuala Lumpur
Tour a scenic Cameron Highlands tea plantation and stop in the royal town of Kuala
Kangsar
See top attractions in Penang, including UNESCO-listed Georgetown and Fort
Cornwallis
Visit Kek Lok Si — the Pagoda of 10,000 Buddhas — and the cave temple of Sam
Poh Tong
Experience the wet market of Kota Bharu and the heritage waterfront city of Kuala
Terengganu
Marvel at replicas of famous world monuments at the Islamic Civilization Park, situated on Wan Man Island
Hotel pickup and drop-off included, with optional upgrades for airport transfers available on Days 6 or 7
expect: Experience the beauty of Malaysia’s coastal villages, cultural attractions, religious temples and historical landmarks on this seven-day Best of Malaysia Tour with stops in Cameron Highlands, Penang, Kota Bharu and Terengganu. This trip popular trip includes round-trip coach transportation from the capital city, as well as accommodation. Travelers can opt for a late evening flight (own expense) on day six from the Kuantan airport or return by coach to Kuala Lumpur on day seven.

(Upgrades that include airport transfers are available.) Personalize your trip by choosing from single, twin or triple-accommodations with 3-, 4- and 5-star hotel options. Breakfast buffets included, as well as plenty of time to enjoy the amenities at each of the unique resorts. Itinerary
Day 1: Kuala Lumpur – Cameron Highlands

Start with pickup from your hotel or meet your guide at Corus Hotel Kuala Lumpur, departing for the Cameron Highlands in the morning. You’ll drive a distance of 137 miles (220 km), stopping en route to see a local basket-weaving cottage industry, followed by a visit to Lata Iskandar Waterfall and a native settlement. Your knowledgeable guide accompanies your group to each location and offers interesting commentary on cultural and geographical features along the way.

Upon arrival at Cameron Highlands, one of Malaysia’s largest hill stations, you’ll be immersed in wondrous landscapes along the northeast side of the Pahang Mountains. Here, at an elevation of 5,060 feet (1,542 meters), the gentle slopes of the highlands offer cool temperatures and crisp air.

Your tour along this scenic plateau — well-known for its tea estates, farmland, rivers, lakes and orchards — includes a visit to a tea plantation, tea factory, market and butterfly farm. In the evening, sip tea on a large, private balcony as you relax and take in the views overlooking beautiful gardens. Your fine hill resort, situated on 7 acres (2.8 hectares), offers a mountain-rustic yet elegant atmosphere. Classic but contemporary rooms are furnished with teak furniture and have modern bathrooms with black granite flooring. Overnight: Strawberry Park Resort in the Cameron Highlands
Day 2: Cameron Highlands – Penang (B)

After a buffet breakfast, hop aboard the coach in the early morning. During the 205-mile (330-km) scenic drive to Penang, make a stop in Gunung Rapat to visit Sam Poh Tong, said to be the largest cave temple in Malaysia. As your guide accompanies you up the 246 steps to the top, hear about the legend of the 19th-century Chinese monk who discovered the cave. Your climb is rewarded with a scene of beautifully carved Buddha statues interspersed among the cavern’s stalactites and stalagmites.

Make a second coach stop in the royal town of Kuala Kangsar, where the impressive golden- domed exteriors of Ubudiah Mosque and Istana Iskandariah (the Royal Palace) provide unique photographic opportunities. After visiting the former royal residence of Istana Kenangan, which today houses the Royal Museum of Perak, continue on to the Kuala Sepetang mangrove forest. Considered Malaysia’s best-managed mangrove forest, Kuala Sepetang serves an essential ecological role in protecting the coastline from erosion. Following a stroll along a boardwalk with your guide through the natural mangrove forest, you’ll visit a charcoal kiln where the bulk of the nation’s top-quality mangrove charcoal is produced.

Located on the northwest coast of Penang Island, your hotel makes use of a beachfront setting at the quieter end of the lovely Batu Ferringhi (Foreigner’s Rock) beach. The resort overlooks a tranquil and scenic bay, and each spacious room includes a private balcony. Enjoy entertainment and recreational amenities, including an outdoor swimming pool, tennis court, spa and fitness center. Overnight: Bayview Beach Resort in Penang
Day 3: Georgetown, Penang (B)

Leaving your hotel by coach after breakfast, drive to historical Georgetown, located just 25 minutes away. Upon arrival at the UNESCO World Heritage site, embark on a comprehensive sightseeing tour with your guide to see Georgetown’s top cultural attractions. View the third-longest reclining Buddha figure in the world, followed by a visit to Kek Lok Si Temple, also known as Pagoda of 10,000 Buddhas.Climb the steps to the temple and explore the area, which includes a magnificent bronze statue of Guanyin, the Goddess of Mercy, and a seven-story pagoda featuring 10,000 alabaster and bronze Buddha statues. Continue by coach to Fort Cornwallis, the landing site of Captain Francis Light when he arrived in 1786 to start the first British colony in Penang. Inside the fort walls there are original, century-old structures like the chapel, prison cells and munitions storage, as well as bronze cannons and flagstaffs belonging to the English East India Company. Then head to the waterfront village of the Weld Quay Clan Jetties, one of the last remaining old Chinese settlements on the island, where you’ll find houses built on stilts along the planks. Driving along Pitt Street, also known as the Street of Harmony, view the churches, Chinese temples, mosques and Hindu temples that have stood side by side for centuries in harmonious coexistence. Visit the intricate Khoo Kongsi clan house — part of a close-knit network of Chinese clan associations established in Malaysia in the mid-19th century. Finally, enjoy a breezy trishaw ride, still a popular mode of transport in Georgetown. Pass charming colonial buildings and modern skyscrapers before returning to your hotel to spend the rest of your day at your leisure. In the late evening, feel free to explore the nightlife along Batu Ferringhi. Overnight: Bayview Beach Resort in Penang
Day 4: Penang – Kota Bharu (B)

Following breakfast, depart Penang for Kota Bharu, a distance of approximately 250 miles (400 km). Journey east across Peninsular Malaysia through the main mountain range, which offers breathtaking views of the dense tropical rainforest while you travel through villages and plantations.

En route to your destination, make a photo stop on Banding Island with its scenic lookout over the picturesque Temenggor Lake. Enjoy the calm lake surrounded by the immense rainforest — a perfect spot for a lunch break at a hotel restaurant with window views (own expense).

Farther, on, your coach stops at the highest mountain point along the route; located 3,445 feet (1,050 meters) above sea level, this overlook offers impressive vistas of the forested Titiwangsa mountain range as well as Thailand over the Malaysian border. On arrival in the state of Kelantan, proceed to the border town of Rantau Panjang, a popular meeting and trading point for the people of both countries. From the Malaysian side of the border, look for Thai villages across the Golok River — a lifeline for residents on both sides, as it provides the water supply for daily and agricultural use.

If you’d like, peruse a variety of products at the duty-free shops before settling in for the evening in Kota Bharu at your Marriott accommodation, the only 5-star international hotel in town. Choose from several dining options at the hotel’s restaurants or lounge, enjoy the pool or fitness center, or head to the spa for ultimate relaxation. Overnight: Renaissance Kota Bharu in Kota Bharu
Day 5: Kota Bharu – Kuala Terengganu (B)

Start your day with breakfast, followed by a visit to the colorful wet market of Kota Bharu and the area’s traditional cottage industries, such as silver handicrafts and songket weaving. Then reboard the coach for a 105-mile (170-km) drive south along the scenic coastline toward the heritage waterfront city of Kuala Terengganu. Taste some keropok, the popular local chips made of fish or prawns, before checking in to your hotel. The remainder of the day is yours to spend at your leisure.
Overnight: Felda Residence Kuala Terengganu
Day 6: Kuala Terengganu – Kuantan (B)

Check out of your hotel after an early breakfast to embark on a 155-mile (250-km) journey by coach toward your next destination, Kuantan. First, stop en route to visit Pulau Duyong (Duyong Island), famous in the region for its traditional boat making. Accessible via a bridge, the island village involves a bit of walking with your guide, who shares interesting facts about the boats’ construction — they’re created without metal nails — as you watch a master boatman at work.

The Islamic Civilization Park, situated on Wan Man Island, is another must-see local attraction. The theme park showcases 20 replicas of the world’s great Islamic monuments, such as Spain’s Alhambra citadel, the Taj Mahal of India, the Masjid-al Haram of Saudi Arabia, Jerusalem’s Dome of the Rock and many more. Your guide ensures that you visit the iconic Grand Crystal Mosque, the highlight of the park.

Continue with a visit to a brassware-making center before heading farther south toward Cherating in the district of Kuantan. Your coach stops at a scenic coastal fishing village where you tour a sea turtle information center to learn more about these endangered species. En route, taste lemang, rice cooked with coconut milk in bamboo — a popular Malay specialty not to be missed — followed by afternoon tea hosted by the local community. Cherating’s main attractions include a village resident’s entertaining monkey that is trained to pluck coconuts from a tree, and a visit to a local cottage industry, where you can see mengkuang leaves being weaved into bags and mats.

After this bit of sightseeing, you can relax at your world-class beach resort, located on the pristine shoreline of Balok Beach. Gaze at the cobalt waters of the South China Sea from your private balcony, stroll the lush green garden or retire under a coconut palm. Refresh in the outdoor free-form swimming pool and hot tub, or head to the Samsara Spa for a full range of treatments. You’ll find plenty of gourmet delights as you dine in elegant surroundings or head to the bar for a cocktail under a lush canopy of trees. (Spa, drinks and dining options are your own expense.) If you prefer not to stay overnight and travel overland back to Kuala Lumpur the next day, you may schedule a flight from Sultan Ahmad Shah Airport in Kuantan, departing anytime after 8:30pm. Airport drop-off is available with your upgrade. Overnight: Swiss Garden Resort and Spa in Kuantan
Day 7: Kuantan – Kuala Lumpur (B)
After breakfast, you’re driven back to Kuala Lumpur, a distance of 168 miles (270 km). Hotel drop-off is included, or upgrade to a transfer to Kuala Lumpur International Airport

title.en: Pulau Ketam Village Tour from Kuala Lumpur Including Thean Hou Temple

overview: Discover the laid-back fishing village of Pulau Ketam (Crab Island) during this 8-hour excursion that also includes a short sightseeing tour in Kuala Lumpur. Experience the daily lifestyle of the the island’s locals as you explore this unique community situated above the water line on stilts. Then enjoy a tasty Malaysian lunch before catching the included ferry back to Kuala Lumpur, where you’ll undertake a brief coach sightseeing trip to two of the country’s largest mosque and Chinese temple. Your excursion also includes round-trip hotel transport, a guide and entrance fees.
highlights: Discover the simple lifestyle in the quaint fishing village of Pulau Ketam on this tour from Kuala Lumpur
See how houses and roads of this rustic community are built on stilts!
Witness daily activities of fisherman and residents
Savor authentic Malaysian flavors with lunch at a local restaurant (own expense)
Visit two of Malaysia’s most famous religious landmarks: Sultan Salahuddin Abdul
Aziz Mosque and Thean Hou Temple
expect: Experience both the rural and urban sides of Malaysia during this morning visit to the fishing village of Pulau Ketam, followed by a ferry ride back to Kuala Lumpur to visit the country’s largest mosque and Chinese temple. It’s a great way to get a sense for the unique contrasts of tradition, religion and modern urban areas that make Malaysia such an interesting melting pot. Begin your trip with a pickup from your central Kuala Lumpur hotel. Pickups will begin prior to 8:45am, so expect details from Nobles Tours during reconfirmation of the exact schedule. You’ll then proceed on a 1-hour drive to the ferry terminal at Port Klang to catch your boat to the small fishing hamlet of Crab Island (Pulau Ketam). After arriving on the island, set off on foot to begin your exploration of this one-of-a-kind community built on stilts above the waters of the area’s mangrove swamps. As you walk you’ll witness some of the key differences in daily lifestyle between the city dwellers and the island’s residents. Observe locals as they take a break on their front porches, walk past brightly-colored Chinese temples adorned with statues of marine creatures and spot fishermen as they peel shrimp for consumption in the local restaurants. As you might expect of this coastal city, Pulau Ketam is famous for its seafood, particularly crab. Stop by a local restaurant to have some lunch (at your own expense) savoring the strong, vibrant flavors of Malaysian cuisine, a culinary style that blends a variety of cultural influences. After your meal, catch your included ferry back to Port Klang, where you’ll begin a short coach sightseeing tour of Kuala Lumpur.

Drive first to the ornate Palace of the Sultan of Selangor before heading to the Sultan Salahuddin Abdul Aziz Mosque. At almost 36 acres (15 hectares) the second largest such mosque in Southeast Asia and the biggest in Malaysia.

Make your final stop of the day at Thean Hou Temple, also among the largest in Southeast Asia. Check out the temple’s complex murals and many decorative details, providing a great example of Chinese artistic techniques. From here you’ll receive a drop-off back at your central Kuala Lumpur hotel.

overview: Get a bird’s-eye view over Kuala Lumpur from the Observation Deck of the 88-story Petronas Twin Towers. This private tour with a professional driver-guide takes you sightseeing around the city as well as to Batu Caves. Visit sites of historical value such as Merdeka Square (Independence Square) and the National Mosque, and shop at Central Market or the Royal Selangor Visitor Center. Then head to Batu Caves and climb the 272 steps to its Hindu shrine.
highlights: Private sightseeing tour of Kuala Lumpur and Batu Caves
Take in the city skyline from the Petronas Twin Towers Observation Deck
Admire the architecture of Merdeka Square (Independence Square), home to the
National Museum
Visit the Lake Gardens and shop at Central Market or the Malaysian Batik Center
Snap photos of the Old Railway Station, National Monument and National Mosque
See statues of Hindu gods at the impressive Batu Caves
Hotel pickup and drop-off included by private vehicle
expect: Start your day by visiting one of the most iconic buildings not only in Kuala Lumpur, but in Malaysia in general. You’ll be taken to the Petronas Twin Towers in a comfortable vehicle with a private driver and professional guide. You will enjoy one of the best views you’ve ever seen as you go up to the observing deck of Petronas Twin Towers and take in the magnificent skyline along with the city lying before your eyes.

You will then move on to Merdeka Square (Independence Square) for a photography, its diverse architecture and a whole green field right at the center, followed by the Istana Negara (King’s Palace), that has a great view with gardens, pools and fabulous courts. The National Museum is also a must-see with its extensive collections of traditional costumes, ancient and modern art, archeological exhibits and huge dioramas.

We will visit the Lake Gardens and enjoy a moment away from the hustle and bustle of the city. At the Central Market, you can enjoy not only fresh local food, but also a great variety of souvenirs, batik masterpieces, jewelry, and paintings. A visit to the Malaysian Batik Center will let you get a glimpse of how these wonderful fabrics are created. We will drop by the Royal Selangor Visitor Center and let you buy some of the finest pewter souvenirs, which make by magnificent alloy. You will also make a stop near the Old Railway Station to marvel at its intricate Moorish styling with columns, arcs and verandas, and then move to the National Monument and the National Mosque, which was built as a staggering religious and spiritual symbol of Malaysian independence.

Kuala Lumpur is not all about modern buildings and monuments, another sight for you to admire is located inside a huge limestone cave. The Batu Caves are one of the biggest historical and religious Hindu sights that attract both tourists and believers that wish to marvel at the impressive shrines and take in the calm and peaceful atmosphere. There’s also a remarkable statue of Lord Muruga at the entrance and two more caves with carvings and shrines for you to explore.
Finally, you’ll be taken back to the hotel to enjoy a relaxing evening after a wonderful trip.

title.en: Kuala Lumpur Heritage Walk

overview: Take a walk through the historic heart of Kuala Lumpur and discover its cultural heritage on this half-day tour, including food tastings. Join a knowledgeable guide who shares insight about the former tin mining settlement and its diverse inhabitants. Stroll through the oldest neighborhood in the capital and stop to sample authentic foods. You’ll also see where different communities worship at several temples.
highlights: 4-hour heritage walking tour of Kuala Lumpur with a local guide
Stroll through Central Market and Chinatown
Get a look at Sin Sze Si Ya Temple and Sri Mahamariamman Temple
Learn about enduring traditions of Chinese and Indian immigrants
Sample authentic Malaysian food
Small-group tour ensures personalized attention
expect: This tour offers the perfect opportunity to learn about Kuala Lumpur’s history and culture. This tour has been designed to appeal to anyone aged 11 and over who consider themselves foodies or culture buffs.
Your day will begin at 9am at the Be Tourist Information and Service Center, Central Market Annexe.

On this tour, you will experience hearing tales of the first Chinese and Indians in Kuala Lumpur, shop at the Central Market (Pasar Seni), visit Chinatown, be inspired by the Sin Sze Si Ya Temple, marvel at the Sri Mahamariamman Temple and also be able to enjoy eating delicious authentic Malaysian food.
The tour will end at 1pm at Lebuh Ampang.

title.en: Private Tour: Cultural Night of Kuala Lumpur with Dinner and Show

overview: Join this night excursion and get experience the nightlife of Kuala Lumpur. You will visit the famous night bazaar of china town for bargains and sights. Then take a short tour to Sri Mahamariamman Temple and Petronas Twin Towers for photography. Enjoy the delightful array of local Malay cuisine where you will enjoy a traditional Malay culture performance.
highlights: See the sights illuminated at night
Get inside tips from a local
Dinner included
Family friendly

expect: The tour will starts by visiting the bustling night market in Chinatown and try your skills at bargaining. Chinatown is still one of the liveliest meeting points of the city with its stalls and its restaurants spread over several small streets. You will also see the Sri Mahamariamman Temple, one of the most ornate Indian temples where you may even get to see a Hindu wedding if you are lucky.

After experiencing the hustle, bustle and excitement of Chinatown and the Sri Mahamariamman Temple you really have been showcased the cultural diversity of Malaysia. We then go to a local restaurant and you will be served a delicious Malay dinner. After dinner you will enjoy a traditional Malay cultural performance. A photo-stop at the Petronas Twin Towers, the famous twin skyscrapers in the heart of Kuala Lumpur City Center. The towers are illuminated during the evening hours - a scenery which will make you stand in awe for the sophistication of its architecture. You will be transported back to your hotel after the tour.

title.en: Private Day Trip to Malacca from Kuala Lumpur

overview: On a private day trip from Kuala Lumpur, get to know the historical city of Malacca, a UNESCO World Heritage site.
Learn about the city’s multicultural heritage and trading history as you check out attractions like St Paul’s Hill, Stadthuys and Jonker Street. Enjoy personalized attention from a private guide.
highlights: Private Malacca day trip from Kuala Lumpur
Visit the World Heritage–listed sites of Malacca City
See remains from the city’s Portuguese and Dutch rule
Go shopping on Jonker Street
expect: After pickup in Kuala Lumpur, your day trip starts with the approximate 2-hour drive to Malacca City, where you’ll first visit Stadthuys, a remnant of the city’s Dutch history built in 1650.

Next, head up to St Paul’s Hill for a view of the city and to see St Paul’s Church, which dates back to 1521, making it one of the oldest churches in Southeast Asia. Take a break for lunch (own expense) before continuing your tour to Jonker Street, located in Chinatown and known for its abundant shopping opportunities. Browse antique shops and craft outlets for gifts and souvenirs, and perhaps try a dessert known as chendol, shaved ice with red beans, coconut milk, palm sugar and green jelly.

Visit the ruins of A Famosa, a Portuguese fortress and one of the oldest remains of European architecture in the region. Make a stop at Cheng Hoon Teng, a Chinese temple that practices three doctrines: Buddhism, Confucianism and Taoism. Your day trip then ends with the drive back to Kuala Lumpur.

title.en: Lotus Leaves Painting in Kuala Lumpur

overview: Unleash your inner artist during a 3-hour lesson on painting lotus leaves. Use leaves of various sizes to create each masterpiece of color for your home or office; these acrylic paintings make lovely souvenirs, gifts and delightful conversation pieces about your time in Kuala Lumpur. This small-group workshop runs with a maximum of five students per class to ensure personalized attention from your instructors, who offer materials and guidance.
highlights: 3-hour painting workshop in Kuala Lumpur Spend time painting on lotus leaves in harmonizing colors Materials including acrylic paints, canvas, packaging and DIY varnishing kit are provided Small-group class is limited to five students
expect: Simple painting techniques will be demonstrated to get you started and your friendly facilitators will be right there with you; providing guidance at any moment you need throughout the workshop. Don’t fret over making mistakes because the beauty of lotus leaves painting is that you can simply do them over. So let loose your inhibitions and set the infinite palette of your imagination free Experiment with colors fearlessly and watch as every brush stroke unfolds a beautiful new layer into something stunning that is uniquely yours. Rest assured that you’re in good hands with our facilitators who will provide you with everything you need in terms of guidance and tools. You will be completely at ease during this fun and highly interactive workshop. Lotus leaves painting is about the harmonization of colors and tones, so here are some helpful tips given during the lessons. Please feel free to bring photos, books, items or materials that you feel may help your color creativity during the workshop. We will be on hand to prompt you in the right direction!
You will have a choice of various sizes of canvases and all you need to do is choose which size you would love to paint on at the beginning of the workshop.

title.en: Private Half-Day Putrajaya Tour with Lake Cruise from Kuala Lumpur

overview: Explore a city of Putrajaya, Malaysia third and latest Federal Territory with our professional English speaking guide on this private half-day tour. This is a model garden city with several interesting places you can visit, such as the Pink Mosque, Agricultural Heritage Park and we cruise on the beautiful Putrajaya Lake. We offer 2 departure times to suit your schedule, 9am or 3pm with round-trip transfer from your hotel in Kuala Lumpur and Petaling Jaya.
highlights: Choice of morning or afternoon departure
Private tour is operated with just your party and a guide/driver
Travel by boat and see the sights from the water
Great overview and orientation of the city
Instant Confirmation
Ideal choice for families
expect: Our driver will pick you up from your hotel in Kuala Lumpur around 9am or 3pm by a private air-conditioned vehicle and head to the federal capital of Malaysia, Putrajaya. Country’s Administrative Center and it was named after its first Prime Minister, Tunku Abdul Rahman Putra.

Relax and enjoy the scenic 45-minute drive from Kuala Lumpur. Your first stop on this 4 hour tour will be at the Taman Warisan Agricultural Heritage Park, which is a living museum of fruit, rubber, cocoa, palm oil, herbs, and more. See a demonstration of the rubber manufacturing process from the point of tapping the tree.

Afterwards, you’ll continue on to see some of Putrajaya’s most famous landmarks, including the pink-domed Putra Mosque. Fashioned from beautiful rose granite, the monument rises 250 feet into the air and is one of the tallest landmarks in the region. Next you’ll visit Perdana Putra, the prime minister’s office. Known as the White House of Malaysia, this imposing building is home to several key government agencies.

Enjoy a short cruise across Putrajaya Lake and admire the beautiful scenery. Before making your way back to your drop off point, you’ll pass by the Sepang Formula 1 Race Circuit that’s widely recognized as one of the top circuits on earth.

title.en: Kuala Gandah Elephant Sanctuary and Batu Caves Tour from Kuala Lumpur with Lunch

overview: Enjoy a day away for the hustle and bustle of Kuala Lumpur city with our day trip to Kuala Gandah Elephant Sanctuary. This trip offers you the opportunity to get to know each of the orphanage elephants and gain a special understanding of their daily lives and behaviours. We will visit to Batu Caves which is an iconic and popular tourist attraction in Selangor. Lunch and hotel transfer in Kuala Lumpur city area is included.
highlights: Close encounter with wildlife
See native wildlife in their natural environment
Lunch included
Enjoy a day away from the hustle and bustle of the city
Family friendly
All taxes, fuel surcharges and service fees included
expect: This trip starts by pick you up at your hotel lobby in Kuala Lumpur city area at 9am. We will head to the first stop Batu Caves. Batu Caves is a Hindu Temple located at the outskirt of Kuala Lumpur city. These limestone caves are 400 million years old and there is a total of 272 steps leading up to the top of the main cave temple. It consists of three big caves. The world's tallest Lord Muruga Statue with the height of 42.7m (130 feet high) is located here. We will then move on to Lanchang town for lunch (local cuisine) will be served and drive through rubber / palm oil plantations, Malay Traditional houses and Aboriginal village. After lunch, we will continue our journey to Kuala Gandah Elephant Conservation Centre. Activities start by feeding the orphanage elephants followed by watching the staff bathing the adult elephants in the river. You may join to bathe and play with the elephants in the river (if weather and river water level permits). You will get change and clean up(for those had gone into the river) before head back to your hotel in Kuala Lumpur after an unforgettable experience.

title.en: Half-Day Batu Cave and Kuala Lumpur Countryside Tour

overview: Enjoy a half day trip to the limestone hills of Batu Caves that comprises of three caverns and several smaller caves, a Hindu deity – a flight of 272 steps lead up to the temple cave. Another cave, called the museum cave, is filled with images of deities and murals depicting scenes from the Hindu scriptures.

expect: Enjoy an adventure journey to the spiritual Batu Caves which located north of Kuala Lumpur, and climb the 272 steps carved into the sides of giant limestone cliffs to reach the Hindu temple at the summit. Then, visit the Batik Center to experience traditional Malaysian cloth- dying, used as sarongs and fabric.

Your first stop is the energetic Little India district, where you discover the delicacies of Indian culture through the colorful food stalls and markets selling everything from saris to golden trinkets.

Leave the hustle and bustle behind as you reach the 400 million-year-old Batu Caves. Follow in the footsteps of pilgrims before you and brave the climb to reach the temple with many Hindu shrines. On the way back down, snap a few photos of the mischievous monkeys. Your next stop is the Malaysian Batik Center, where authentic batik fabric is designed and produced into ready-to-wear material. Your final stop before returning to Kuala Lumpur is the Royal Selangor Pewter Center, where you see the world’s largest pewter company at work and can pick up some splendid souvenirs.

title.en: Half-Day School of Hard Knocks and Royal Selangor Pewter Tour

overview: Get hands-on experience with one of Malaysia’s most iconic products with a half-day tour of the pewtersmithing workshop at Royal Selangor Pewter.

Learn about the history and design of pewter as you watch expert craftsmen on the factory floor, then use a hammer and wooden mold to create your own dish. Start by using your tools to shape the dish, then move to a decorative workshop to create intricate designs and buff your work to a high polish. Take home your dish and an official pewtersmithing certificate.
highlights: Half-day tour and pewtersmithing workshop from Kuala Lumpur
Enjoy a hands-on experience
Learn the secrets behind Royal Selangor Pewter
Take home a handmade souvenir
Family friendly
Free hotel pickup and drop-off included
expect: You’ll be picked up from your hotel in Kuala Lumpur and taken to the Royal Selangor Pewter. Upon arrival at the Royal Selangor Visitor Centre, you’ll be met by the house guide for a guided tour. Tour a house with more than a century of history. Founded in 1885, Royal Selangor is a well-known name in quality pewter, a brand synonymous with design and craftsmanship. In the hands of skilled craftspeople, this versatile alloy of tin, copper and antimony is transformed into an endless variety of homeware and gifts sold in more than twenty countries around the world. The Visitor Centre takes you back over a hundred years to the founding of Royal Selangor and its inextricable link with the history of Malaysia, to the present day as the world’s largest pewter maker and its expansion into gold and sterling silver.

title.en: Kuala Lumpur Shore Excursion Mah Meri Sea Gypsies Cultural Village with Coconut Wine and Lunch

overview: Be immersed in the historical traditions of Malaysia during a private shore excursion to a ‘kampong,’ a typical indigenous village. When your ship pulls into the cruise terminal, be chauffeured by your own personal guide who shares insightful commentary. Witness the lifestyle of the Meri Meri people, taste coconut wine, take an herb garden tour and enjoy a typical Malay lunch at a family home. Round-trip transport from Kuala Lumpur’s Port Klang is included.
highlights: Lunch included
Led by a local guide
Family friendly
All entrance fees included
Snacks and Beverages included
Enjoy a day away from the hustle and bustle of the city
expect: At 8am, you will be meet and greet at the Cruise Terminal in Port Klang where all cruise ships usually dock. An allowance of 2 hours is given for meet and greet due to dock congestion. Depart to a quaint village and meet the indigenous Senoi tribe of aborigines the Mah Meri who were sea gypsies depending on fish agriculture and now excel in wood carvings depicting rich mythological meanings with spiritual connections. Still remaining 2,000 of them to keep their culture going.The village guide will show us around not forgetting the Rumah Moyang Ancestral Home where food and drinks are offered to the ancestors in return for protection from evil. A simple wood carving and origami awaits. At 11:30am visit a coconut plantation to watch the tapping of coconut wine (toddy), a practice copied from India. It has an alcohol content of 4% and a health drink. We then proceed to a typical Malay home for an herbal garden tour led by the owner and a delicious home cooked lunch will be served. After lunch, we will drive past scenic houses on stilts with photo shoots along the way. We will stop by at a coconut wine shop for some exotic snacks with a cup of toddy.
Around 4pm, we will depart to cruise terminal.

title.en: Full-Day Mah Meri Cultural Village Experience

overview: Experience Malaysia’s diverse cultures with a 7-hour tour to Mah Meri Cultural Village, an Indian enclave, and some of Kuala Lumpur’s most important sites. Meet members of the Mah Meri community, and learn about the group's religious practices, history and traditional wood carving. Browse colorful shops in Klang town before enjoying an Indian lunch at a local restaurant, and return to Kuala Lumpur by public train. Visit the atmospheric Old Railway Station, then stroll to the National Mosque, Central Market and Merdeka Square, a landmark of colonial-era architecture.
highlights: 7-hour cultural tour from Kuala Lumpur
Learn about life in the Mah Meri Cultural Village
Explore a historic Indian enclave
Enjoy an Indian lunch in a local restaurant
Take a walking tour of Kuala Lumpur's sights
Hotel pickup included
expect: At 8:30am, depart for an hour journey to Mah Meri Cultural Village, also known as the village of the Mask Man of Malaysia. An up-close personal experience with the Mah Meri indigenous tribe, they are 1 of the 19 indigenous tribes in Peninsular Malaysia. Learn and have an insight into their animistic and superstitious beliefs and a close view of their beautiful handiwork. You will be welcomed by a traditional welcome ceremony before you are invited into the village. Then, you will be able to visit galleries and there will be short video about the history of the tribe. After that, you will be taken for the village tour to see the temple and a place where they do wood carving. Next, they will take you to see where they make origami, and you will be able to learn the art of making the ancient form of palm leaf origami to appease the spirits and for you to keep as a souvenir. You will be provided with light refreshment after the tour before heading to the next destination. The tour will then proceed to Klang Town for the Little India enclave along Jalan Tengku Kelana, Klang known as the biggest Indian street in Malaysia. Fierce competition among shop owners translate into cheaper prices for consumers. Be spoiled by the range of choice with rows of shops on the left and right sides of the road, and stalls spilling onto the sidewalks and back lanes. Myriads of items such as saris, colorful accessories. Enjoy a local Indian lunch before proceeding to the train station for your transfer back to Kuala Lumpur. Take the journey back on public train and get off at the Kuala Lumpur Old Railway Station, which is another major landmark of the country. Continue on foot for a photo stop at the National Mosque before we head to Central Market, which used to be Kuala Lumpur’s biggest wet market. Continue walking to Independent Square. Along the way, you will able to view the birthplace of Kuala Lumpur - at the confluence of 2 rivers in Klang Valley and the oldest mosque in the Kuala Lumpur, Jamek Mosque. Upon arrival at Merdeka Square, view the Tudor-styled Royal Selangor Club and the Mughal inspired Sultan Abdul Samad Building. Tour ends at Merdeka Square.

title.en: Kuala Lumpur Heritage Food Tour

overview: Savor Malaysian cuisine and hear stories about the country’s culinary heritage on this half-day food walking tour with a knowledgeable local guide. Stop by the food stalls of Central Market, walk past the shops of Little India (Jalan Masjid India) and visit Kampung Baru’s local markets. You’ll discover treasured family recipes, nostalgic childhood favorites and fragrant regional dishes. Food tastings included.
highlights: 4-hour food walking tour of Kuala Lumpur with a local guide
Visit Central Market, Little India and Kampung Baru
Sample authentic dishes from markets and hawker stalls
Small-group tour ensures personalized attention
expect: This walking tour brings the cuisines of Malaysia past and present to life. In a metropolis filled with fast food and sleek eateries, you can also still enjoy the simple pleasures of foods of days gone by from different traditions and regions around the country. Our first tastings are in the oldest neighborhood of Kuala Lumpur surrounding Central Market where the same restaurants and stalls have been feeding hungry locals and visitors for generations. From there we move on to Jalan Masjid India, a bustling commercial street packed with snacks and street foods laced with the heady aroma of distinctly Indian spices. Then we take a short monorail trip to Kampung Bahru, or the “New Village” in Malay, originally settled by Malay farmers in the 1890s. We'll shop in the local markets filled with fresh produce and pass historical wooden homes down leafy lanes on our way to sample a host of local delicacies that have their roots in the north and east of the country. The tour is a delicious way to discover the people, places, traditions and flavors that make up Malaysia. Makan makan! Let's eat!

title.en: Kuala Gandah Elephant Sanctuary Tour from Kuala Lumpur

overview: Nature lovers will appreciate the natural wonders of this small-group tour to Batu Caves and the Kuala Gandah Elephant Conservation Centre. Marvel at limestone caves in Gombak, then learn about elephant rehabilitation and relocation efforts at the elephant sanctuary. You’ll get up close to these majestic giants with opportunities to feed them and watch them bathe in the river. Picnic lunch plus round-trip hotel transport is included from Kuala Lumpur.
highlights: Small-group tour of Kuala Gandah Elephant Conservation Centre
Learn how rangers rehabilitate and relocate wild Asian elephants
Stop by Batu Caves to explore the Hindu shrines

expect: Kuala Gandah Elephant Sanctuary is Malaysia premier Elephant Conservation Center and easily accessible for nature lovers. Visitors are allowed to come into close contact with one of the world’s most majestic creatures. Situated approximately two hours from Kuala Lumpur city center. The early history was set up by Malaysian Wildlife Society, it is the base of operations of the Department Of Wildlife and National Parks Elephant Relocation Team, which assists in the capture and relocation of rogue elephants from across Southeast Asia. Departing at 9am, our first stop out of the city is at the iconic Batu Caves in Gombak. An important place of worship for Hindu devotees in Malaysia, this natural attraction is made up of a series of limestone caves said to be more than 400 million years old. The towering golden statue of Lord Muruga is regarded as the tallest statue of a Hindu deity in Malaysia. Guarding the entrance of the main cave it glints ethereally against the cloudy sky. Two cave temples called Art Gallery Cave and Museum Cave are also contained in the main complex, as well as a Tamil school, several souvenir shops and vegetarian eateries. We are then ushered into an air-conditioned audio-visual theater for a 25-minute video documentary on the National Parks Elephant Relocation Team’s conservation activities and programs. The informative presentation allows us to have a better understanding of the work conducted at the center, the duty of the team’s trained elephants and the highly hazardous responsibility of the rangers when they are out in the field conducting wild elephant relocations.

We take a five-minute walk to the elephant enclosure where five rehabilitated elephants are kept. Visitors can feed these elephants by purchasing sugar canes, bananas, and peanuts from a stall nearby. Soon after, the elephants are led towards a nearby river where they are groomed and bathed by professional handlers. For an additional charge, visitors can experience the thrill of bathing with the elephants, all under watchful eyes and careful supervision.

The Kuala Gandah Elephant Sanctuary Tour is a great way to escape the hustle and bustle of Kuala Lumpur city, get back in touch with nature, as well as discover the important roles that the elephant sanctuary play in ensuring the survival and well being of these majestic animals.

overview: Explore the UNESCO World Heritage-listed city of Malacca on a full-day tour from Kuala Lumpur. You will then drive past the largest 17th century Chinese cemetery outside of China, located at Chinese Hill (Bukit China). There will be a short stop at the foothill so you can view the Sultan's Well before driving through the Portuguese Settlement. You will proceed to view the famous gateway Porta De Santiago and the ruins of St Paul’s Church which is lined by 17th century Dutch tombstones.

Next on the list is the Red Square - the salmon pink Dutch administrative building which today houses the Malacca Museum and some other government offices. You will then be taken to see Christ Church.

After Christ Church you will enjoy a delicious lunch at a local restaurant. After your lunch, you will be taken to visit the Adobe of the Green Merciful Clouds (Cheng Hoon Teng Temple). title.en: Full Day Cameron Highlands Tour

overview: See one of Malaysia’s most renowned hill stations on a full-day Cameron Highlands tour from Kuala Lumpur.

Travel to the cooler hilltop regions where tea plantations carpet the mountains. Visit BOH tea plantation to learn about tea production, and stop at other highlights such as Sam Poh Temple in Brinchang and Tanah Rata. Visit a strawberry farm to pick fresh strawberries, a typical vegetable market and the gardens of Cactus Valley. You’ll enjoy sweeping views of the emerald green scenery throughout this jewel of a region.
highlights: Full-day tour to Cameron Highlands, from Kuala Lumpur
Tour the BOH tea plantation
Pick fresh strawberries and stop at a vegetable market
Visit the towns of Brinchang and Tanah Rata

See the cactus collection at Cactus Valley
expect: Cameron Highlands was named after the discoverer William Cameron in 1885, a British government Surveyor who came across, "A fine plateau with gentle slopes", while he was researching through dense jungle on a mapping expedition. Creating a hill station in the area was first voiced in 1888 by Sir Hugh Low, a Perak resident who propose the idea it might be a suitable place for a retreat and farmland. Cameron Highlands was a heaven for the British who were stationed in Malaya as it provided relief from the hot and humid tropical climate of the lowlands.

Cameron Highlands stands at 1524 meters (5000 feet) above sea level, enjoys a cool climate, with temperatures rarely higher than 25°C and low than 10 °C. In 1929, John Archibald Russell, who was the son of a British administrative officer started a tea plantation which is now the famous BOH Tea Plantation. BOH stands for Best of Highland. The other tea plantation was established in 1932, by the Shuparshad family and known as Bharat Tea Plantation in Cameron Valley brand. You will have chance to learn and understand the tea processing.

Cameron Highlands is the nation's prime producer of fresh vegetables as well such as cabbage, chili, cauliflower, broccoli and tomatoes. The strawberries and flowers are successfully cultivated and are the main export to Singapore. You can also self-pluck your strawberry from the tree.

Cameron Highlands is the smallest district in Pahang, nestled between the State of Perak and State of Pahang, covering an area of 443 square kilometers. It is positioned close to the border to the north. It is made up of 3 main township at different elevations. The first town you'll see coming from the South is Ringlet, followed by Tanah Rata and Brinchang. There are few small town such as Tringkap, Kuala Terla and Kampung Raja which going towards Northern part of Malaysia.

title.en: Full Day: Heritage Tour of Malacca from Kuala Lumpur

overview: Experience the charms of Malacca, situated on the Straits of Malacca. Let an informative guide reveal the multicultural history on this heritage tour of the World Heritage–listed colonial town. See the architecture and religious traditions of Indian and Chinese immigrants, sample local Malaccan specialties and visit Porta de Santiago (A Famosa), which dates back to Portuguese traders. Minivan transport is included from central Kuala Lumpur.
highlights: Malacca heritage tour from Kuala Lumpur
Visit significant landmarks such as Porta de Santiago (A Famosa)

expect: Malacca (or Melaka in modern Malaysia) has always been a strategic crossroad between east and west. When the Sultanate of Malacca fell to the Portuguese in 1511, it became the first European outpost on the Straits of Malacca.

Over the centuries, the Dutch replaced the Portuguese and the British replaced the Dutch, while the port's key role in trade across Asia brought immigrants from China and India, as well as Malays. Chinese and Malay traditions merged to form what is known today as Baba Nyonya culture; Indians and Malays formed the Chitty community. Each group maintains its own beliefs and traditions and a vibrant blending of cultures that is typically Malaccan. The city is host to Malaysia's oldest Chinese and Hindu temples and the country's oldest Catholic Church.

Other highlights of the tour include the grand Baba Nyonya houses along Heeren Street and Jonker Street's quaint storefronts, the Dutch architecture of Stadthuys or “Red” Square and the sites of St Paul's Church and the A Famosa fort, both of which date back to Portuguese times. The tour also features Malacca's living heritage, the traditional trades that endure despite the city's rapid modernization. You'll also enjoy the unique flavors of delicious Malaccan food along the old streets of the city.

Stroll past blooming plants in the manicured butterfly park, then visit gardens dedicated to orchids and hibiscus. Enjoy the serenity of the historic park, whose lakes, gardens and animals are a sanctuary from Kuala Lumpur’s busy streets.

title.en: Rice Fields and Fireflies Tour including Lunch and Dinner from Kuala Lumpur

overview: This full-day itinerary showcases the surroundings of Kuala Lumpur, from the Sekinchan rice fields to the Kuala Selangor Nature Park mangroves. Along the way, you’ll visit Pantai Redang (Redang Beach), a rice museum and several temples. Top off the tour with a boat ride past fireflies lighting up the night forest. A seafood lunch and riverside dinner are included with round-trip hotel transport.
highlights: Kuala Lumpur day trip to Sekinchan rice fields
Learn about rice production with a knowledgeable guide
Stop by Redang Beach and Nan Tian Temple
Ride a boat through the mangroves and firefly habitat of the Kuala Selangor Nature
Park
