expect: This Sekinchan Rice Field and Kuala Selangor Fireflies Tour starts at 10am from Kuala Lumpur. Our journey starts with a 90 minute drive through the Kuala Lumpur countryside, passing a Palm Oil plantation and a jungle. On the way we stop off at a Chinese temple and a famous wishing tree. We then arrive at the beautiful Redang Beach before heading to Sekinchan for a fresh and tasty seafood lunch.
Sekinchan is a well known fishing village and one of the major rice supplying regions in Malaysia.

After lunch we take you to the Sekinchan rice fields, depending on the time of year the colors of the fields can vary from whether they are in the planting or harvesting season. We then visit the Rice Museum to learn more about the history of this major rice producing area. On our way out of Sekinchan we visit the beautiful Nan Tian Temple and with the sun starting to set we continue to Melawati Hill, a former fort with a antique cannon facing the busy Straits of Malacca. Whilst here it is likely you will encounter the local inhabitant, the Silver Leaf Monkey.

We then proceed towards Kuala Selangor for dinner and your boat ride through the mangroves. Our seafood dinner is served on the riverside and if you are lucky enough to see it the sunset view is amazing. Once dinner has finished and night is upon us we join our boat to view the fireflies. You will be amazed by these mesmerizing fireflies and the area is known to have one of the largest colonies in the world. We then head back to your hotel in Kuala Lumpur.

overview: Venture into the countryside outside Kuala Lumpur and learn about cultural traditions with a Mah Meri guide who provides insight on Malaysia’s aboriginal seafarers — a subgroup of the Senoi belonging to the Orang Asli people. This day trip takes you to the tribal region of Carey Island where you’ll experience a slower pace of life. After a personal tour of the village, visit a coconut plantation for a taste of homegrown toddy, or coconut wine. Lunch and round-trip hotel transport are included.
highlights: Full-day Malaysian countryside tour including Mah Meri aboriginal village
Let a Mah Meri aboriginal guide lead a comprehensive tour
Lunch, snacks and coconut wine tasting are provided
Hotel pickup and drop-off included
expect: This tour showcases the older tribal areas of the Mah Meri aborigines. A Mah Meri Guide will take you on a comprehensive tour of the village. The tapping of coconut wine was a practice that was copied from India and other parts of the world. The drink, which has an alcohol content of 4%, was popular with the Indian laborers in Malaysia as it was quite affordable to them. The tapping of this wine is slowly being faced out.

The tour will starts after breakfast around 8am, and departs for the countryside. You will arrive at the Mah Meri Village after an approximately 2-hour drive. Mah Meri guide will take you on a tour of the village, explaining their culture and traditions. After visiting the Rumah Moyang (Ancestral Home), move on for a demonstration of wood carving. Around 12pm, visit a coconut plantation to watch coconut tree climbers harvest a unique drink - the coconut wine (toddy). Toddy is a health drink that cleanses the urethral and liver systems. Fresh toddy is served at the plantation.

Next, visit a typical Malay home for an herbal garden tour of traditional plants for blood pressure, cancer, diabetes and other ailments. A delicious home cooked meal will be served. After lunch, drive past scenic villages and houses on stilts with photo stops along the way. Then its time for a toddy party, fresh toddy and some snacks such as wild boar, chicken and mutton, before departing for Kuala Lumpur and arriving approximately 5pm.

title.en: Full Day Taman Negara Tour from Kuala Lumpur

overview: Trekking for 2 hours in the rainforest of Taman Negara — home to many threatened animal species including tigers, elephants, tapirs, rhinos and sun bears — is just one of several adventures offered on this day trip from Kuala Lumpur. On arrival, see the treetops on a canopy walk and learn about the abundant flora and fauna with your nature guide. You'll get onto the river and shoot the rapids then watch a blowpipe demonstration at an Orang Asli aboriginal village. Lunch and transport included.
highlights: Taman Negara day trip from Kuala Lumpur
Learn about hundreds of plant and bird species on a 2-hour rainforest trek
Embark on a canopy walk and visit an Orang Asli aboriginal village
Lunch and round-trip hotel transport provided
expect: Your day will start early with a 7.00am pick up from your centrally located Kuala Lumpur hotel. We will then embark on the three and a half hour long drive to Kuala Tahan. Along the way you can enjoy the scenery of Kuala Lumpur.
Upon arrival, at approximately 10:30am, the fun will begin. Enjoy some packed snacks at the forest.

Get your adrenaline pumping with the Canopy Walk! It is the longest canopy walkway in South East Asia with a bird's eye view of stunning scenery of the world's oldest rainforest. Enjoy trekking to the Teresek Hills. The experienced nature guide will belt out facts and fancies of the varied flora in Taman Negara. He will uncover secrets and taboos of the forest. Let out your inner-adventurer at the Rapids Shooting. Rapids Shooting is a thrill, as the boatman negotiates 7 sets of rapids. It is a take-home experience as there is a "chance" to get wet.

Immerse yourself in the culture with the Aborigine village visit. The "orang asli" are of the batek tribe who have been living environment friendly lives. The rainforest is their supermarket where they get their life's necessities. A fire making and blowpipe demonstration is the order of the day.

Be sure to come with good walking shoes, insect repellents, and a change of cloothing. At approximately 4pm we will return to Floating Café for some lunch and freshening up before departing for Kuala Lumpur.

Have time to shop or take in the sights before continuing to Cheng Hoon Teng, a Chinese temple that combines three doctrines: Taoism, Buddhism and Confucianism.

title.en: Private Tour: Ipoh Old Town Food Tour from Kuala Lumpur

overview: Swap the bustle of the capital for the charming colonial town of Ipoh on this full-day tour, including round-trip train transport from Kuala Lumpur. Make the most of your private guide and flexible itinerary as you take in the highlights of the historic center on foot. Marvel over landmarks like Kellie’s Castle and the Perak Tong temple, then discover the town’s gastronomic heritage as you browse the markets and sample an array of street food and authentic Malay dishes.
highlights: Full-day private food and cultural heritage tour of Ipoh
Travel round-trip by train from Kuala Lumpur with a knowledgeable private guide
Walk to hawker stalls, food courts and markets for food tastings with authentic Malay dishes
Delight your senses with curry noodles, barbecued fish and aromatic white coffee
See colonial landmarks such as the Ipoh Railway Station, Ipoh Town Hall and the
Birch Memorial Clock Tower
Visit Kellie’s Castle and Perak Tong, a Buddhist temple in a limestone cave
expect: Meet your guide at KL Sentral railway station in Kuala Lumpur and board an express train to begin your full-day tour. The 2.5-hour train ride takes you north to Ipoh; once a thriving commercial center during the tin-mining boom of the 19th century, the charming town now serves up local favorites at food stalls, food courts and restaurants. Start your culinary adventure with a stroll through Ipoh’s streets in search of breakfast. Follow your guide on foot and savor the best food available, from Ipoh sar hor fun (rice noodles served with sweet sauce) to melt-in-your-mouth kaya puffs (flaky pastry filled with egg jam On a short heritage walking tour, visit historical buildings constructed during the British colonial era.Take a break and sip a cup of Ipoh’s freshly brewed, aromatic white coffee before heading 3 miles (5 km) north of town to Gunung Lang. This recreational park features a gorgeous lake situated amid limestone outcroppings. Located a short distance away is Perak Tong, a cave temple that houses more than 40 Buddha statues, including a 42-foot-high (13-meter) centerpiece. If you climb the 385 steep steps to the top you’ll be rewarded with stunning views of the surrounding countryside — a photographer’s heaven! Stop by Kellie's Castle to see the unfinished mansion perched atop a hill where it was built on a former rubber estate in Perak, before returning to Ipoh for lunch. Continue your food tour on a walk to local markets and hawkers stalls, feasting on Malay dishes served up with white rice. Enjoy favorites such as barbecued fish marinated in a savory sauce; chili chicken; locally grown vegetables authentically cooked using coconut, shrimp or chili paste; curry noodles; barbecued pork; dim sum; and fried green onions. After tasting some sweet treats such as cendol — a traditional dessert made from shaved ice, coconut milk, green starched noodles and sugar — stop by a nearby pamelo farm to sample this citrus fruit native to Southeast Asia.

Visit a kacang putih factory to sample a variety of these popular snacks, including fried beans, crispy tapioca chips and murukku (savory, crunchy twists made from rice), which are original to Ipoh and shipped worldwide. Learn how the industry began in the 1940s from just six families who settled in the city from South India.

title.en: 4-Day Taman Negara Adventure From Kuala Lumpur

overview: Delve deep into the Malaysian rainforest on this 4-day Taman Negara adventure from Kuala Lumpur. Spot native nocturnal wildlife during a forest night-walk with your guide. Paddle upstream to Lata Berkoh and test your nerve on Malaysia’s longest suspension bridge. Hike up Teresek Hill to Mount Tahan and enjoy stunning views over the dense forest below. Swim in the Lubok Simpon water hole or spot wildlife from a secret hide. Meet local tribe members at the Orang Asli settlement, then splash through thrilling rapids on a white-water rafting trip.
highlights: 4-day, 3-night trip to Taman Negara from Kuala Lumpur
Stay three nights at the Mutiara Taman Negara Resort, in the heart of the rainforest
Take part in various activities offered at the resort, including the popular canopy walk and the night jungle walk
Learn about the aboriginal lifestyle on a visit to the Orang Asli settlement
Feel your heart racing while shooting river rapids
Look for native wildlife like wild pigs, tapirs, sambar deers and more!
expect: Day 1 (D) Your trip starts with a three-hour drive from Kuala Lumpur to the river bank at Kuala Tembeling. Here, board a motor canoe for the two-hour ride to your resort. Enjoy the sights and sounds of the rainforest as you cruise along the river. Once settled in, join expert resort guides for a night walk through the rainforest. Try to spot a few creepy crawlies hiding in the dark!
Day 2 (B,L,D) Today is activity day around Taman Negara – choose from a variety of outdoor experiences that will bring you closer to nature.

Take a canoe upstream to Lata Berkoh, where you can go fishing – there are an estimated 300 species of fish in the river! Tackle the longest suspension bridge in Malaysia – more than 1,700 feet (500 meters) – on the canopy walk. Hike up Teresek Hill to Mount Tahan, where you’ll be rewarded with breathtaking views of the park. Go swimming at the Lubok Simpon water hole. Or join park guides on an ‘Animal Vigil’ in a tree house to look for wildlife. Day 3 (B,L,D) Connect with aboriginals on a visit to the Orang Asli settlement. Learn about the native culture from local residents and discover their semi-traditional way of life, from playing the blowpipes and hunting with bows and arrows to using medicinal plants and building shelters with bamboo, wood and palm leaves.

Later in the day, put on your lifejacket for a thrilling river rapids experience to Kuala Trenggan. As you ride along the river on a wooden boat accompanied by experienced boatmen, you’ll shoot through the many rapids and become quite drenched! Day 4 (B) Breakfast ends your Taman Negara experience. You will be taken by boat and coach back to Kuala Lumpur, where you can reminisce about your amazing, one-of-a-kind adventure!

title.en: 3-Night Cameron Highlands and Penang Tour from Kuala Lumpur

overview: See the best of Malaysia’s rural highlands on this three-night Cameron Highlands and Penang Tour from Kuala Lumpur. Enjoy round-trip coach transportation from your hotel or airport, as well as luxury accommodation on this memorable journey beyond the urban landscapes. A professional local guide will lead travelers through a tea plantation, the famed Sam Poh Tong cave temple, the historic city of Georgetown and the Kuala Sepetang mangroves. Enjoy an upclose look at the Kek Lok Si Temple, as well as a traditional trishaw ride on this one-of-a- kind tour that showcases the highlights of this unique nation!
highlights: 3-night tour of Cameron Highlands and Penang from Kuala Lumpur
Tour a tea plantation and butterfly farm with an informative guide
Visit the cave temple of Sam Poh Tong and the Pagoda of Ten Thousand Buddhas
— Kek Lok Si
See Lata Iskandar Waterfall, Fort Cornwallis and the Clan Jetties of Weld Quay
Stop at Khoo Kongsi, a historical Chinese clan house in Penang’s Chinatown
Ride a trishaw through Georgetown, a UNESCO World Heritage Site
Hotel pickup and airport drop-off included
expect: Your three-night Cameron Highlands and Penang Tour from Kuala Lumpur kicks off with coach transportation from your hotel or the airport. Enjoy a scenic ride through rural Malaysia, as well as overnight accommodation at the Strawberry Park Resort—home to incredible views and rustic mountain atmosphere. Choose from single, twin or triple-share room options, which all include large private balconies, perfect for relaxing. In Penang, you’ll enjoy two night’s at the Bayview Beach Resort, just north of Penang Island. The beachfront locale on Batu Ferringhi offers a dramatic departure from the rolling hills of Strawberry Park Resort. Enjoy views of Foreigner’s Rock, as well as luxe rooms with private balconies. Accommodation includes tennis courts, fitness center, spa and swimming pool to enjoy at your leisure Itinerary
Day 1: Kuala Lumpur – Cameron

Highlands Departing around 8:30am with pickup from your hotel in Kuala Lumpur, board your comfortable coach for the 135-mile (220-km) drive to the Cameron Highlands, one of Malaysia’s largest hill stations. Stop along the way to see a cottage industry of local basket weaving, followed by a visit to Lata Iskandar Waterfall and a native settlement — all accompanied by commentary from your knowledgeable guide. The gentle slopes of the Cameron Highlands, nestled in the northeast side of the Pahang Mountains, boast wonderful scenery amid crisp air and cool temperatures. Situated 5,060 feet (1,542 meters) above sea level, the tableland or plateau is well noted for its tea estates, farmlands, rivers, lakes and orchards. Your day tour here includes a visit to a local tea plantation, tea factory, market and butterfly farm.
In the evening, settle in at the luxurious hill resort, enjoying views from the balcony as you sip your tea.
Overnight: Strawberry Park Resort in the Cameron Highlands
Day 2: Cameron Highlands – Penang (B)

In the early morning, set off after breakfast for Penang aboard the coach and enjoy the scenic 205-mile (330-km) drive. En route, visit Sam Poh Tong, an impressive cave temple in Gunung Rapat, said to be the largest in Malaysia. Once you’ve climbed the 246 steps to the top, your guide will point out beautifully carved statues of the Buddha interspersed among the stalactites and stalagmites. Hear the legend of the 19th-century Chinese monk who discovered the cave and learn how the temple was later constructed.

Make another coach stop at the royal town of Kuala Kangsar for the opportunity to photograph the stunning golden-domed exteriors of Ubudiah Mosque and Iskandariah Palace. View the former royal residence of Istana Kenangan, which today houses the Royal Museum of Perak.

Proceed further to the Kuala Sepetang mangrove forest, the best-managed mangrove forest in Malaysia, serving an important ecological role in protecting the coastline from erosion. Delight in the novelty of walking with your guide through the natural mangrove forest along a boardwalk. As Kuala Sepetang produces the bulk of the nation’s top quality mangrove charcoal, you’ll also visit a charcoal kiln where charcoals are produced. In the late afternoon, you’ll cross over into Penang via Penang Bridge. Spanning eight miles (13.5 km) across, it’s one of the longest bridges in the world! After checking in to your hotel, feel free to relax or explore the nightlife along Batu Ferringhi. Overnight: Bayview Beach Resort in Penang
Day 3: Georgetown, Penang (B)

After breakfast, depart by coach from your hotel and embark on a comprehensive sightseeing tour of historical Georgetown, located just 25 minutes away. Your guide will lead you to top cultural attractions in Georgetown, declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site. View the third longest reclining Buddha figure in the world, followed by a visit to Kek Lok Si Temple, also known as Pagoda of Ten Thousand Buddhas.Climb the steps to the temple, which includes a magnificent bronze statue of Guanyin, the Goddess of Mercy, and a seven-story pagoda featuring 10,000 alabaster and bronze Buddha statues.

Continue by coach to Fort Cornwallis, the landing site of Captain Francis Light when he arrived in 1786 to start the first British colony in Penang. Inside the fort walls there are original structures like the chapel, prison cells, munitions storage, bronze canons and flagstaff belonging to the English East India Company.
Then head to the waterfront village of the Weld Quay Clan Jetties, one of the last remaining old Chinese settlements on the island, where you’ll find houses built on stilts along the planks.

Driving along Pitt Street, also known as the ‘Street of Harmony,’ view the churches, Chinese temples, mosques and Hindu temples that have stood side by side for centuries in harmonious existence. Visit the intricate Khoo Kongsi clan house — part of a closely-knit network of Chinese clan associations established in Malaysia since the mid-19th century. Finally, enjoy a breezy trishaw ride, still a popular mode of transport in Georgetown. Pass charming colonial buildings and modern skyscrapers before returning to your hotel to spend the rest of your day at your leisure.
Overnight: Bayview Beach Resort in Penang
Day 4: Penang (B)
After checking out of your accommodation, you’ll be transferred to Penang International Airport, located approximately 50 minutes away.

Please note that the tea factory closed on Monday and public holidays. Lunch will be served around 1pm and then check out. We will visit Butterfly Farm, Strawberry Farm, Vegetable Market, the Cactus and Flower Gardens. At 4pm, we depart for Kuala Lumpur and arriving approximate 5pm, en-route visit Batu Caves before heading back to your hotel.

title.en: 3-Day Taman Negara Adventure from Kuala Lumpur

overview: Take a walk on the wild side and explore one of the world’s oldest rainforests on this 3-day Taman Negara adventure, including 4-star accommodation, meals and transfers. Cruise down the Tembeling River by motor canoe, then get a taste of local life as you pass traditional ‘kampongs’ and take a jungle survival class. Keep a lookout for colorful birds, monkeys, tapir and wild boar as you enjoy a thrilling night hike through the jungle, then get an aerial view during a treetop canopy walk.
highlights: Kuala Lumpur to Taman Negara 3-day trip
Scenic, two-hour boat trip from Kuala Tembeling to Kuala Tahan
Walk across the canopy walkway to see the forest from a unique vantage point

2-night stay in a 4-star resort hotel and expert guide included
expect: Day 1: Kuala Lumpur - Kuala Tembeling - Taman Negara (L, D)

Depart from Kuala Lumpur for a three-hour drive to the rural town of Jerantut. Here, you’ll stop for lunch and a short rest before proceeding to Kuala Tahan. From here, enjoy a short boat ride to the park headquarters. Along the way on this scenic journey, you’ll see kampongs (Malaysian wooden houses), local fishermen, monkeys and jungle vegetation. Arrive and enjoy your evening of leisure After dinner (included in tour), watch a video presentation giving an overview of Taman Negara and embark on a night jungle walk with park rangers. You’ll explore the jungle from a different perspective and possibly see nocturnal animals. Overnight: 4-star Mutiara Taman Negara Resort or similar
Day 2: Taman Negara (B, L, D)

The itinerary for day two may vary depending on the season and availability of the park facilities. A common activity is to walk along the canopy walkway. The canopy is suspended 82 feet (25 meters) above the ground between massive trees and allows for close-up views of the higher reaches of the forest. After the canopy walk, go on a jungle trek to Teresik Hill. From here, you’ll be able to view Mt Tahan, the highest mountain in peninsular Malaysia, soaring to 7,186 feet (2,178 meters). During the trek, you’ll learn about the fundamentals of jungle survival, jungle ecology and flora identification from your guide. Returning back to the park headquarters on a different trail, you’ll pass Lubok Simpon water hole where you can jump in for a swim. At night, you’ll have the option to participate in an animal 'vigil' at the tree house. However, sighting of animals is not guaranteed.
Overnight: 4-star Mutiara Taman Negara Resort
Day 3: Taman Negara - Kuala Lumpur (B, L)
After breakfast, you will take the return journey to Kuala Lumpur.

title.en: 2-Day Private Tour of Malacca from Kuala Lumpur

overview: Discover traditional culture and colonial heritage in Malaysia on this private 2-day tour of Malacca from Kuala Lumpur. Visit palm oil and rubber plantations with your private guide. Spend time in a local village to learn of local customs and heritage, and enjoy free time to explore bustling Malacca at your leisure. Admire top attractions including Stadthuys and the Porta de Santiago, and climb St Paul’s Hill for fine views over the beautiful Strait of Malacca. Visit the town’s oldest functioning Taoist temple and delve into Chinatown’s vibrant Jonker Street.

Learn about Malacca's Portuguese and Dutch influences on a guided city walking tour

expect: Day 1: Kuala Lumpur - Malacca

To begin your 2-day tour, you will be picked up from your Kuala Lumpur hotel for a 2-hour (approx.) drive to Malacca. Your guide will take you first to the outskirts of Malacca to discover what life is like outside the main town. Listen to your guide’s knowledgeable commentary as you pass by rubber and oil palm plantations, paddy fields and quaint Malay villages (kampongs) with houses built on stilts. Stop at Morten Village, a typical Malay kampong that still displays old Malay customs, such as constructing houses on stilts Arrive in Malacca and check into your hotel. Afterward, the rest of the night is yours to explore Malacca at your leisure or relax in your hotel.
Overnight: Equatorial Hotel or similar in Malacca
Day 2: Malacca - Kuala Lumpur (B)

After breakfast, your private guide will take you on a walking tour of the city center rife with historical monuments. Visit Stadthuys, known as the Dutch Square, as it was built in 1650 by Dutch occupants. Walk past Porta de Santiago, one of the surviving gates of the historic A’Famosa Portuguese fortress. Walk up St Paul’s Hill for a panoramic view of the Strait of Malacca and the old town of Bandar Hilir. Atop the hill, see the ruins of St Paul’s Church, lined by 17th-century Dutch tombstones.

Follow your guide on a 15-minute walk to Cheng Hoon Teng, Malacca's oldest functioning Taoist temple, with prayer halls boasting rich decors. Then, stroll along the lively pathways of Jonker Street in the heart of Chinatown, where vendors are selling various souvenir items and local delicacies.

At your guide’s suggestion, choose to have lunch at a local restaurant (own expense) in any of the towns you pass on your way back to Kuala Lumpur. You’ll arrive back at your hotel in Kuala Lumpur by late afternoon or early evening.

title.en: Monkey Feeding and Firefly Evening Tour from Kuala Lumpur

overview: Participate in a feeding frenzy during this up-close encounter with the silvery lutung, also called a silvered leaf monkey or silvery langur. Offer the monkeys green leaves and fruits and watch as they clamber all over you! After your own dinner at a riverside cafe, ride a boat to view fireflies as they shimmer and shine in the night, putting on a spectacular show. This day trip to Bukit Melawati, located in Kuala Selangor, includes hotel pickup and drop-off from Kuala Lumpur.

expect: Your tour will begin with a pickup from your hotel before departing Kuala Lumpur at 4pm for the fishing village in Kuala Selangor. Upon arrival at the Bukit Melawati Hills in Kuala Selangor at approximately 5:30pm, you will visit the lighthouse perched 27m (88.6 feet) above sea level. You will also have the opportunity to come face to face with the adorable Silvered Leaf Monkeys.

The Silvered Leaf monkeys are adorable and friendly animals that live on the Bukit Melawati Hills. These monkeys live on shoots, young leaves and wild fruits. They tend to live in clusters of 6 to 10 and their infants are orange in color, often turn silver after 3 months. You will be provided with snacks such as green leaves and fruits to feed to the Monkeys. Prepare for a close encounter with nature at its best as the Monkeys may climb all over you to reach the food!
After this special experience, you will be taken to a riverside cafe for a delicious dinner, all fresh from the fishing village.

After dinner, you’ll catch a boat to watch the fireflies. You must remain quiet, so as not to scare them away. The sparkling lights of the fireflies resemble a Christmas tree. It’s a beautiful, natural phenomenon and also quite rare in this part of the world. The Fireflies congregate on mangrove trees to feed on nectar. They flash synchronously and the light is produced by a complex biochemical reaction in their light organs situated on the underside of their bottoms.
At approximately 8:30pm you will depart for your hotel in Kuala Lumpur. At 10pm you’ll arrive safe and sound with many new memories to cherish.

The 88-floor towers have a facade of steel and glass that distinctly reflect images of Islamic Art. Designed by a South American architect, the base of Twin Towers houses a shopping mall and the Malaysian Philharmonic Orchestra. You will then visit Lake Gardens (Perdana Botanical Garden), with some beautiful trees, man-made waterfalls and playground. We will stop at a war memorial the National Monument. It is a huge bronze statue, muscular in nature, with warriors defending the wounded and fallen.

National Mosque (Masjid Negara), a magnificent structure that is a unique embodiment of modern Islamic art with stunning traditional elements. We will explore Kuala Lumpur Railway Station, a lovely majestic palace once nearby the National Mosque. Chinese Thean Hou Temple, built in the classic style of Mainland China. Being one of the oldest and greatest temples in Southeast Asia, this landmark attracts millions of tourists from across the globe each year.

If you are more into shopping than sightseeing, you can easily omit any of these places and go for a fascinating journey into the depth of Central Market, where you can spend your time looking through artwork, souvenirs, and batik masterpieces. Chinatown, filled with countless Chinese shops is an ideal place to hunt for everything from cheap spices to gadgets. Little India is a small Indian island inside the bustling streets of Kuala Lumpur. Here you can try fantastic Indian dishes, look for bright saris and enjoy the glittery stalls filled with trinkets and jewelry of all kinds.

The second most desired visiting place in Kuala Lumpur is the Batu Caves. Dedicated to Lord Murugan, this Hindu shrine holds a magnificent 155ft (47meter) statue erected in his honor. 272 stairs lead to the massive Temple Cave with a spectacular 328ft (100meter) high ceiling. The cave is filled with statues of Hindu gods and intricate paintings illuminated by the holes in the rock of the ceiling.

It is also possible to visit the Royal Selangor Pewter Factory and Visitor Centre where one can delve into the process of pewter manufacturing and learn about its properties, while enjoying the fascinating pewter museum located on the premises of the factory. You will dropped off back to your hotel after finishing the tour.

You will also visit the six-tiered Chinese landmark of Thean Hou Temple built to match some of the temples in Mainland China, a grand structure that never fails to impress tourists with its architecture. The final stop and drop off point of your sightseeing tour of Kuala Lumpur is the KL towers and you will be pleased to know that your entrance ticket for the observation deck is included in this tour.

title.en: KL Tower Observation Deck Admission Ticket

overview: Enjoy sweeping views over Kuala Lumpur from the KL Tower Observation Deck. The enclosed deck provides 360- degree views, and your admission ticket includes a multisensory movie experience at the XD Theater. You can also upgrade your ticket to add a stop at the Open Deck, which perches more than 1,000 feet high at the top of the tower.
highlights: Admission to KL Tower Observation Deck in Kuala Lumpur
See Kuala Lumpur from one of the highest spots in the metropolitan area
Enjoy panoramic views from the enclosed deck
Have fun watching a multisensory movie at the XD Theater
Upgrade for the Open Deck admission to enjoy views as far as the Genting Highlands and South China Sea
expect: The KL Tower (aka the Menara Kuala Lumpur) is one of the most iconic sights in Kuala Lumpur and is visible from most parts of the city. It's one of the world’s tallest telecommunications towers, a major tourist destination and a popular venue for special occasions.

The tower sits on a hill, making it appear taller than the city's famous Petronas Towers; KL Tower measures 1,381 feet (421 meters) high while the Petronas Towers measures 1,483 feet (452 meters). With your admission ticket, you may visit whenever you wish during operating hours. Perhaps go to watch the sunset and see lights come on across the sprawling city below. When booking, choose from the following two admission options. KL Tower Observation Deck and XD Theater:

After arriving at KL Tower, take one of the high-speed elevators up to the fully enclosed Observation Deck, located 905 feet (276 meters) above ground level. The deck circles the entire tower, providing panoramic views of Kuala Lumpur.

Also included is admission to the XD Theater for a 6D-movie experience. Watch the movie while seated in a specially designed armchair that moves in sync with the film. The combination of visual and sound effects, seat movement and other features makes you feel like you're in the middle of the action on screen. There are typically about eight movies that you can watch, and each film runs for about five minutes.
KL Tower Observation Deck, XD Theater and Open Deck:

Upgrade your admission to include all of the above plus a ticket to the Open Deck, which perches at the top of the tower, 1,381 feet (421 meters) above the ground. The open-air deck offers a spectacular perspective of the Kuala Lumpur skyline, with views that extend to the Genting Highlands, Pahang and South China Sea.

After this wet and wild escape you’ll understand why Sunway Lagoon ranks tops among Malaysia’s amusement and water parks. This detonation is jam-packed with more than 80 attractions and three theme lands. Head into the park, where you’ll find some 80 attractions and multiple theme lands to explore: World of Adventure, Extreme Park, Wild Wild West, Scream Park and Waters of Africa. title.en: Dinoscovery and Aquaria KLCC Admission with Round-Trip Transfer

overview: Marvel over some of the world’s most awe-inspiring creatures, both past and present, on this unique 4-hour tour of Kuala Lumpur’s Aquaria KLCC and Dinoscovery by Dinosaurs Live. First journey back to the dinosaur age and learn all about the prehistoric creatures through interactive exhibits and animatronic displays. Next, venture beneath the ocean at the huge aquarium, complete with an underwater tunnel, touch pools and piranha-feeding displays. This tour includes admission to both attractions, round-trip transfers and around four hours to explore both independently.
highlights: Admission to Dinoscovery by Dinosaurs Live and Aquaria KLCC
Pretend to be a paleontologist on a scavenger hunt for dinosaur bones during Dino
Quest
Learn about the Age of Dinosaurs with more than a dozen life-size, animated displays
Observe tiger sharks, seahorses, piranhas, otters, electric eels and more
Visit streams, coastlines, flooded forests and open sea via numerous exhibits
Includes round-trip hotel transport
expect: Meet your driver upon hotel pickup in the morning or afternoon and transfer to Avenue K Shopping Complex. Here, gain admission to Kuala Lumpur’s latest family attraction, Dinoscovery by Dinosaurs Live.

Travel 250 million years back in time to the Mesozoic era and learn about the Age of Dinosaurs at this interactive exhibition with more than 15 life-size animatronic dinosaurs. See how the prehistoric beasts moved and hear them roar as you learn about their habitat and the climate conditions that contributed to their extinction.

This sprawling, 13,000-square-foot (1,208-square-meter) space is packed with numerous educational and entertaining activities, suitable for the entire family. Dino fans can watch a short documentary in the 3D cinema, climb a 16-foot (5-meter) wall to peek into a pteranodon’s nest, or be a paleontologist searching for unique specimens like a triceratops’ footprint during a scavenger hunt called Dino Quest.

Next, depart to Aquaria KLCC for the ocean discovery portion of your tour, where you can explore the mysteries of the sea without having to leave the city. Lovers of aquatic life will enjoy a visit to this gigantic aquarium, situated in the basement of the Kuala Lumpur Convention Centre.

Reputed to be one of the largest aquariums in the world, Aquaria KLCC covers more than 5,000 square feet (465 square meters) and showcases nearly 150 species of fish from various parts of the world. The highlight of Aquaria is a 295-foot-long (90-meter) transparent underwater tunnel that you can walk through.

Delight in watching sand tiger sharks, 6.5-foot-long (2-meter) arapaimas, coral fish, seahorses and many more. See piranhas, otters and other sea creatures hand-fed daily at a feeding show. Other attractions include snakes, geckos and poisonous dart frogs. (See complete exhibit list under Itinerary below.) When your time is up, your driver will meet you and transfer you back to your hotel. Itinerary Rocky Shore Touch Pool: Observe and feel a sea cucumber, horseshoe crab, gentle bamboo shark and more.
Electric Zone: Learn how animals like the electric eel, electric catfish and elephant-nose fish defend themselves by discharging electricity.
Streams: Visit jungle streams, home to land and aquatic animals such as alligator snapping turtles and Asian small-clawed otters.
Flooded Forest: Be greeted by the radiant glow of thousands of silvery scales of fish swirling within a tubular tank.
Coast: Discover how a mixture of freshwater and saltwater in estuaries provides many nutrients for marine life.

Oceanarium: The vastness of the open sea and the entrancing rhythm of life there are re- created here with giant stingrays, green sea turtles and more. Weird & Wonderful: Walk into the darkness to see delicate and mysterious marine creatures like sea jellies and seahorses.
Glass-Bottom Boat: Take a seat on a simulated boat deck of the Explorer II and discover the wonders that can be seen at ocean reefs.

overview: Escape to the Sunway Lagoon Theme Park with admission, lunch and transfer from Kuala Lumpur. Start the day hassle-free with pick-up at your centrally-located hotel, then explore the park at your own pace. Catch a wave at the largest man-made surf beach in the world and take on the Pirate’s Revenge and the Lost City of Gold roller coaster. Enjoy rides and attractions that are suited to all ages and interests, from Captain Kid’s Playland to a World War Z! zombie experience, with return transfer to your hotel when ready.
highlights: Admission, lunch and transfer to Sunway Lagoon theme park from KL
Enjoy the park at your own pace
Have lunch at the park
Spend your day hassle-free
Popular choice with kids
All taxes, fuel surcharges and service fees included
expect: You'll get two ways transfer to Sunway Lagoon Theme Park from Kuala Lumpur City Center hotels on private basic (PVT). These transfers are between Kuala Lumpur City Center hotels to Sunway Lagoon Theme Park by van (Toyota Hiace or Hyundai Starex). The pickup and drop of services session will be between 9am -7pm daily and the journey duration will be approximately 45 minutes.

Upon your arrival, please collect your entrance ticket at the counter with the assist of your friendly driver cum guide and enjoy your splendid moment in Water Park, Amusement Park, Wildlife Park, Extreme Park and Scream Park. You'll get complimentary food voucher as well.

In Sunway Lagoon Explore world’s largest man-made surf beach with the area over 13,000 sf. It will boost your excitement while catching the perfect wave each time! It is also home to the world’s largest water ride, Vuvuzela, and to First Waterplexx 5D, Malaysia’s first FlowRider, and many other great attractions.

Hop on board Pirate’s Revenge, Malaysia’s first 360-degree Rotating Pirate Ship. Scream your way along the ride on the Lost City of Gold Scream Coaster. Captian kids Playland and Captian Kid’s Candyland are themed playgrounds that are designed especially for kids. Kids will have tons of fun at these 2 newly designed attractions. Challenge yourself at adrenaline-pumping fun at Extreme Park. . Hit the bullseye at the Archery Target Shooting Range, go off-road on an all-terrain vehicle (ATV), or satisfy your need for speed on a go-kart.

Helicopters are waiting to rescue you but to reach them you have to make your way through an industrial complex swarming with zombies. World War Z! Live is just one of the highlights of the Scream Park that features no less than 3 floors of fear! Ground zero is turned into World War Z! Live. This is the latest addition to Lynton V. overview: Head to Sunway Lagoon for a fun day and experience the wonders of over 90 rides and attractions spread across Water Park, Amusement Park, Extreme Park and Wildlife Park. Be afraid as you enter Lynton V Harris’ Scream Park, where great evil resides. Our new Asia’s 1st Nickelodeon Theme Lost Lagoon, you will be enthralled by this lost civilization surrounded by lush, natural rainforest. Skip the line
Instant Confirmation
Ideal choice for families

expect: Sunway Lagoon Water Park:

Beat the tropical heat in the Waters of Africa at Sunway Lagoon Water Park! Go for a spin in the loops of the African Pythons, or race your friends in an adrenalin-pumping ride head first down the Congo Challenge. You can also do the Cameroon Climb, get drop 15 metres then shoot back up 8 metres for prolonged fun. There’s something here for everyone, whether you are young or old, thrill seeker or beach bum.
Sunway Lagoon Amusement Park:

You don’t have to be soaking wet to have fun. Head over to the Sunway Lagoon Amusement Park for a seriously great adventure. See a view like no other when you walk on Malaysia’s Longest Pedestrian Suspension Bridge, or see the world upside down when you spin 360 degrees on the Tomahawk and Pirate’s Revenge. Excitement is the name of the game here! Sunway Lagoon Extreme Park:

This is a shout out to all you adrenalin junkies, thrill seekers and extreme sport fans out there. Gear up for an aerial adventure on Malaysia’s longest Flying Fox and soar to great heights on incredible rides such as the Bungy Jump. Whether you conquer the circuit on a Go Kart or conquer the wild on an ATV, you are bound to get some heart-pumping action at the Sunway Lagoon Extreme Park!
Sunway Lagoon Wildlife Park:

Get up close and personal with more than 150 species of animals from around the world at the Sunway Lagoon Wildlife Park, the first and only fully interactive animal-themed attraction in Malaysia. From learning about various species through our unique Wildlife Encounters, observing the animal’s natural antics in specially created habitats, to getting entertained by our talented animal stars in the Wildlife Theatre, there are educational and interesting activities for the entire family.
Sunway Lagoon Scream Park:

Be afraid, be very afraid as you enter Lynton V Harris’ Scream Park, where great evil resides. You’ll be in for a spine-chilling and hair-raising experience at our live action scare extravaganza where fear is the name of the game. Be warned that this is not for the faint- hearted.
Sunway Lagoon Nickelodeon Lost Lagoon:

Enter its majestic gates and be enthralled by this lost civilization surrounded by lush, natural rainforest. Get ready for a wet and exciting adventure as you explore this fantasyland filled with colossal water rides and water playgrounds, canopy walks and meandering pathways, beautiful waterfalls and recreational camp sites. Set amidst 10 acres of lush tropical rainforest with more than 12 rides and attractions provides a mix of thrill and family friendly fun for fans and visitors of all ages. Behold, Asia’s 1st Nickelodeon Themed Land.

title.en: 2-Day LEGOLAND Malaysia Package

overview: Treat the family to an unforgettable overnight trip to LEGOLAND Malaysia, including accommodation and round-trip transfers from Kuala Lumpur. Enjoy non-stop entertainment with over 40 rides and attractions, including the world’s biggest LEGOLAND water park. Marvel over landmarks like Cambodia’s Angkor Wat recreated out of Lego at Miniland; get your adrenaline pumping on a Lego-themed roller coaster or get creative in the interactive discovery zones. Need a break from all that Lego? Tag on a visit to the Desaru Fruit Farm, followed by a shopping trip at Johor Premium Outlets.
highlights: Overnight tour to LEGOLAND Malaysia with private transportation, from your Kuala
Lumpur hotel or Johor's Senai International Airport
Be amazed by Lego dioramas of Asian landmarks like Thailand’s Wat Arun and
Cambodia’s Angkor Wat at Miniland
Stretch your brain at educational areas where you build Lego robots or test Lego buildings in a simulated earthquake
Cool off in the water park with more than 20 water slides, a wave pool and interactive play areas
Find activities aimed at different ages, from toddlers to older kids and adults, something for everyone in your family!
Tour Desaru Fruit Farm, which grows a variety of tropical fruits and has a mini zoo and bullock cart ride
Shop at Johor Premium Outlets for savings of 25% to 65% on name-brands and luxury goods
expect: Your tour includes round-trip transport from your Kuala Lumpur hotel or Johor’s Senai International Airport (JHB) to LEGOLAND, entrance tickets, and an overnight stay at a 3-star hotel. Explore interactive Lego building areas, rides for all ages and an extensive water park with water slides and play areas.
Before your departure on the second day, you’ll have the option to tour Desaru Fruit Farm before stopping at Johor Premium Outlets en route to the airport or your Kuala Lumpur hotel. Itinerary
Day 1: Your Kuala Lumpur hotel or Senai International Airport – Johor Bahru

After morning pickup from your Kuala Lumpur hotel or Johor’s Senai International Airport (JHB), you’ll be transferred in a private vehicle to your hotel for check-in. After you have put down your bags, your driver will take you to LEGOLAND where you can explore more than 40 rides, Lego building zones and water park slides.

The park is divided into seven theme areas, each with rides and Lego building activities for all ages. Don’t miss the Miniland area, where some of Asia’s best known landmarks have been recreated in Legos. Marvel at the detailed miniatures of the Petronas Twin Towers, Angkor Wat, and the Taj Mahal, among others, that were created from more than 30 million Legos! You’ll be able to bring the animated models to life with the touch of a button. If you’re inspired to splash around, hop over to the water park. With more than 20 water slides and pools and areas suitable for younger or older kids, you’ll find plenty to do. Check out the Build-A-Raft River, where you can build a raft from soft Lego bricks then float on a slow-moving current through the park. Or climb around the Joker Soaker, an interactive playground built in a shallow pool, where kids can shoot water canons and a bucket periodically spills gallons of water on those below!

For a brain teaser, head to the activity stations. The Imagination Station allows kids to build dams, bridges and cities out of Lego then test them against a water current. Or try your hand at building robots in the Lego Technic area.

When you need to refuel, choose from seven different restaurants serving a range of Western and Asian dishes (own expense). You’ll also find several shops that sell Lego sets, individual Lego pieces, costumes and other souvenirs.
After a day of fun at LEGOLAND, you’ll be transferred to your hotel for the evening. Overnight: Granada Hotel (3-star) or similar
Day 2: Johor Bahru – Senai International Airport (JHB) or your Kuala Lumpur hotel
After breakfast, you’ll have free time to spend at your leisure or have the option to take a tour of the Desaru Fruit Farm.

The Desaru Fruit Farm grows a variety of tropical fruits such as starfruit, honey orange, papaya, pineapple, durian and more on 160 acres. Learn about the fruits with an experienced guide who will explain the different plants as you cruise around the farm riding in a bullock- cart or your private vehicle. The Desaru Fruit Farm also has a fish pond, mini zoo and other attractions that you can see during your visit. You may even get to sample some of the delicious fruits grown here!

On the way to the airport or to your Kuala Lumpur hotel, you’ll have time to stop at Johor Premium Outlets where you can shop for bargains on name-brand goods in an outdoor mall. Find discounts from 25-65% off on brands like Adidas, Kate Spade, Polo Ralph Lauren, Samsonite, and Versace. If you need a break, have a snack or lunch at one of the ten restaurants in the mall (own expense).
Afterwards, you’ll be transferred to your Kuala Lumpur hotel or the Johor’s Senai International Airport (JHB).

title.en: Kuala Lumpur City Highlights Tour

overview: See the best of Kuala Lumpur on this morning or afternoon city highlights tour that showcases top landmarks, attractions and sites.

You'll see where Old World meets New World as you follow your guide to the King's Palace and Merdeka Square. Make stops at the National Museum, National Mosque, and other key destinations, plus learn about pewter smithing as you watch local artisans at work. This tour includes round-trip hotel transportation and guarantees a good time!
highlights: 3-hour sightseeing tour of Kuala Lumpur's must-see attractions
Enjoy photo opportunities at the King's Palace, Independence Square and Petronas
Twin Towers — the tallest in the world
Learn about Malaysia's history and culture on a tour of the National Museum and
Thean Hou Temple with a professional guide
Admire the elaborate structures of the National Monument, the National Mosque and the Kuala Lumpur Railway Station
Walk through the Royal Selangor Visitor Center to see flawlessly crafted pewter designs and view crafts at the Central Market
Select a morning or afternoon tour to suit your schedule
Includes coach pickup and drop-off at city hotels
expect: Perfect for first-time visitors, this three-hour tour provides a comprehensive introduction to Kuala Lumpur's famous sights, leaving you with a knowledgeable base for exploring the city at your leisure. Meet your local guide upon pickup from your city hotel in the morning or afternoon, and embark on your narrated tour by comfortable coach. Head to multiple Kuala Lumpur attractions, making photo stops at the King's Palace — a symbol of Malaysian sovereignty — as well as Merdeka Square (aka Independence Square), which features a panorama of fascinating buildings in an array of architectural styles. Your guide offers informative commentary on the city’s growing skyline, whose ultra-modern structures tower above edifices with Indo-Moorish influence. Gaze up at the Islamic geometric patterns on the 88-story Petronas Twin Towers, whose multifaceted walls and twin spires contain thousands of steel and glass panels. Your journey continues with a visit to the National Museum to see historic Malaysian artifacts, from traditional weapons and costumes to modern arts and crafts and musical instruments.

Then, drive past the beautiful Lake Gardens on your way to view the National Monument, commemorating Malaysia's struggle for freedom during World War II. Nearby, admire the modern construction of the National Mosque and the pleasant combination of Eastern and Western architecture of the Kuala Lumpur Railway Station.

Visit the six-tiered Chinese landmark of Thean Hou Temple, a grand structure that combines modern architectural styles with authentic traditional design. At the Central Market, browse a variety of local crafts and perhaps have your portrait sketched if time permits. The final stop on your sightseeing tour of Kuala Lumpur is the Royal Selangor Visitor Center, where you will gain insight into pewter-smithing and see innovative pewter-ware design. Afterward, re-board your coach and end with drop-off at your hotel.

title.en: Full-Day Tour: Kuala Lumpur City Including Kuala Lumpur Tower, Batu Caves and Little India

overview: Experience the best of Kuala Lumpur with a full-day tour of the city’s highlights. Start your day in the iconic Kuala Lumpur tower, then go deep into a limestone hillside to explore the Hindu shrines in the Batu Caves. Watch artisans craft pewter and batik at a pair of souvenir factories, walk the colorful streets of Little India then pause for a traditional lunch in a neighborhood restaurant. Finish your day at the Petronas towers, and snap photos, browse boutiques and visit a chocolate shop before returning to your hotel.
highlights: Full-day tour of the best of Kuala Lumpur
Explore the city's highlights with a local guide
Learn about KL's history, culture and art
Visit Kuala Lumpur tower, the Batu Caves, Little India and Petronas Towers
Fun overview, perfect for first-time visitors
expect: Your day will begin with a pickup from your hotel, before departing for the Kuala Lumpur Tower for a bird's eye view of the city at 9am. It houses the telecommunication and meteorological stations and a revolving restaurant. Your next stop is a photo shoot of the Twin Towers.

Visit the breathtaking Batu Caves. Climb 272 steps to reach the Temple of Hindu Deity, Lord Subramaniam, who is honored during "Thaipusam" in January or February every year. You will also see his 140 foot (42.7 m) statue. Batu Caves is said to be one of the most popular Hindu shrines outside India. Please be aware that you must be dressed appropriately to gain entrance in to the temple. Next, you will visit a pewter factory with a guided tour. See handcrafted souvenir items made out of tin, copper and antimony. You will also stop at a batik design factory to see how hand-drawn and block printing is done on cloth. Next, visit the King's Palace and the National Monument, which is a war memorial for fallen heroes. Visit the Old Railway Station, the Independent Square where Malaysia got her independence from the British on August 31, 1957. In its vicinity is St. Mary's Cathedral - an Anglican Church with the Queen of England as the Patron. The exclusive Royal Selangor Clubhouse is of Tudor-styled design.

You will then continue on for a Little India walkabout and banana leaf lunch (enjoy eating with your fingers!) and complete the day with a visit to a cocoa boutique before returning to your hotel at approximately 4pm.

overview: See the best of Kuala Lumpur’s history and culture with a full-day tour of the city’s highlights. Take in the views from the Petronas Towers, then visit the stunning National Mosque of Malaysia and a monument to the country’s fierce struggle for independence. Explore the elegant façade of the city’s old railway station and pause for photos of the fairytale-like King’s Palace. Go deep into a limestone hillside at the Batu Caves and see sacred Hindu shrines before visiting a local art center and returning to your hotel.
highlights: Full day tour of Kuala Lumpur's highlights
Visit Petronas Towers, the Batu Caves and city landmarks
Capture unforgettable images of a colorful city
Learn about Malaysia's history and culture
Great overview of the city, perfect for first-time visitors
expect: After being picked up from your hotel, your driver/guide will show you the charms of the Malaysian capital that are only known to the locals. You’ll have photo stops at King’s Palace, Independence Square, and at the famous Petronas Twin Towers! Head up to the observation deck of the Twin Towers with your admission ticket, where a guide will provide a briefing about the structure before you take in the spectacular city views. On the tour you’ll see the National Monument, the National Mosque, and the Old Railway Station. Also enjoy a visit to Batu Caves, home to the world’s tallest statue of Lord Murugan! Rising nearly 100 meters above ground, the Batu Caves temple complex comprises 3 main caves and a few smaller ones. The largest, referred to as Cathedral Cave or Temple Cave, has a very high ceiling and features an ornate Hindu shrine. To reach the shrine, you’ll need to climb a steep flight of 272 steps.
After visiting the Batu Caves you’ll stop at a pewter art center, where you’ll have the opportunity to browse for gifts before we take you back to your hotel/chosen drop-off point.

title.en: Batu Caves and Malaysian Crafts Tour from Kuala Lumpur

overview: Escape the urban landscapes and leave the streets of Malaysia’s capital city behind on this Batu Caves and Malaysian Crafts Tour from Kuala Lumpur. Visit one of the nation’s most beloved shrines, located in the Batu Caves, and see how two of the country’s traditional crafts are made during stops at the Royal Selangod Pewter factory and a batik center. Choose from a morning or afternoon tour and enjoy round-trip transportation.
highlights: Morning or afternoon tour to Batu Caves
Take a scenic drive through the countryside outside Kuala Lumpur
Tour the famous Royal Selangor Pewter factory
See how batik fabric is designed and printed
Visit the ancient Hindu shrine at Batu Caves
Choice of morning and afternoon tours
expect: Meet your friendly and professional guide at your Kuala Lumpur hotel and leave the city streets behind as you embark on this Batu Caves and Malaysian Crafts Tour. You’ll pass the famed ‘Ambassador Row’ as you depart the city and make your way to the picturesque countryside.

Pay a visit to the Royal Selangor Pewter Factory, where you’ll see how local artisans fashion handmade pieces using age-old techniques. Learn about casting, filing, polishing and hammering techniques used to produce beautiful works as you tour the factory. From there, make your way to a local batik factory, where expert artisans create stunning masterpieces using fabric, wax and colorful dyes. Learn how this age-old art is produced and watch locals at work using this traditional art form.

After learning about the arts and crafts of Malaysia, head to the limestone hills of Batu Caves. Climb the 272 steps that lead to one of the country’s most incredible religious structures. Visit the temple museum, housed inside the cave, and listen in as your guide shares information and insight about the deities that are represented in the temple murals. Your tour ends with hotel drop off in Kuala Lumpur, after a day filled with Malaysian history, culture and traditions.

title.en: Amazing Night Tour with Tickets to Petronas Twin Tower Observation Deck

overview: See dazzling Kuala Lumpur at night from the Skybridge and Observation Deck of the Petronas Twin Towers. You’ll depart from your hotel in the afternoon for a personalized tour of the city before and after dusk. Stop by Independence Square (Dataran Merdeka) for the perfect photo op and stroll around Chinatown’s night bazaar. Finish with a sumptuous dinner of Malay dishes with a dance performance at the Saloma Theatre Restaurant.
highlights: Evening tour of Kuala Lumpur with dinner and dance show
Snap photos of colonial architecture in Independence Square (Dataran Merdeka)

expect: This fascinating journey begins with a hotel pick up in KL city area and head to an iconic landmarks of Kuala Lumpur – the Petronas Twin Towers. Feel the time freeze all around you, as you gaze down from the height of 1,483 feet (452 meters) at the city of Kuala Lumpur stretched underneath your feet. Don’t forget to take some photos of the night city from the famous Sky Bridge, floating above ground like a magnificent star-ship. Next, we will move to Chinatown night bazaar for shopping and you will find mixed of old Chinese shops in the narrow streets selling shoes, clothing, gadgets, spices and traditional Chinese dishes. Chinatown offers its visitors a possibility to visit the finest examples of Hindu temples that can be found in Kuala Lumpur – the magnificent Sri Mahamariamman temple and the Chan See Shu Yuen temple among others.

After shopping at Chinatown, you will be taken to the Merdeka Square to enjoy the breathtaking views of illuminated night city. Being one of the biggest attractions in Kuala Lumpur, the Merdeka Square is an eclectic synergy of modern architectural designs and classic colonial masterpieces. The 200-meter padang (a green field) for years has retained its status as the largest stretch of greenery that can be found in Kuala Lumpur. Capture unforgettable moments on camera as you pass by the majestic buildings of the Royal Selangor Club and St. Mary’s Church.

Enjoy a delicious dinner at one of the most iconic restaurants in Kuala Lumpur, Saloma Theatre Restaurant offers a wide range of traditional Malaysian dishes, followed by a stunning cultural dance performance. A 1-hour show performed by 18 Saloma dancers will not leave anyone indifferent. Don’t forget to try the delicious Malay kampong-style dishes served tiffin style, and the mouth-watering Nasi Goreng Kampung – fried rice with anchovies and loads of Malaysian spices.
Finally, you will be transferred back to your hotel, where you can relax after a night filled with joy and excitement.

overview: Amateur and professional photographers receive personalized attention on this private half- day tour of Kuala Lumpur. Focus your camera lens over a panorama of the city skyline from two iconic spots: Kuala Lumpur Tower and the Observation Deck and Skybridge at Petronas Twin Towers. Frame the perfect up-close photo at Thean Hou Temple, Merdeka Square, the Old Railway Station and more as you sightsee with your personal guide. Admission tickets included.

Photograph the city from KL Tower and the Petronas Twin Towers

expect: Prepare yourself for a half day filled with lots of photographic opportunities as you start your tour from the Petronas Twin Towers once you get onto the observing deck of the famous SkyBridge. Watch as the city stretches below glittering in the sunlight with all its skyscrapers, palaces and museums.

King’s Palace, or the Istana Negara, is a place like no other. Hundreds of photographers visit it each year to capture the magnificent beauty of this rich-looking mansion and its spectacular architecture. Reminiscent of the England’s Buckingham Palace, it has two guard posts that change every hour. The Merdeka Square is one of the biggest architectural jewels of Kuala Lumpur located in the center of the city. You have the opportunity to take some pictures of modern buildings mixed up with colonial masterpieces in the center of the square. A trip to the Lake Gardens can become a nice break from the hustle and bustle of the busy city. Wander the tracks and trails as you take in all the greenery and freshness of a well-kept park. Don’t forget to photograph the picturesque Orchid Gardens and the National Monument, a symbol of Malaysian freedom, which is located nearby. You will stop by the Old Railway Station to take dozens of pictures as this spectacular structure draws the attention of both locals and tourists with its splendid architecture. Built by colonial architects, this stunning structure strikes its visitors with intricate details in the design, splendid arcs, verandas and vast balconies.

The Kuala Lumpur Tower is another significant sight you’ll capture on your camera. It rises high above the city line and provides one of the most breathtaking views you have ever experienced. Climb the staircase or use an elevator as you go up at the height of 421 meters to enjoy the sight. Built in 1995, this tower can boast a sparkling dome made of glass, which shines brightly when the sun hits it.

Thean Hou Temple is a historical sight you simply cannot miss. Built on top of a picturesque hill, this ancient temple is an eclectic mixture of Daoism, Buddhism and Confucianism, which reflects in its peculiar architecture with red pillars, dragons and prayer rooms. The temple is dedicated to the Goddess of Mercy, it also has a Thean Hou shrine and sculptures representing the Astrological animals. You can even have a fortune-reading here! As the tour comes to its end, you will be transported back to your hotel safely.

Head to your first stop, the Orchid Garden, part of the Lake Gardens area (formally known as Perdana Botanical Garden). Check out 3,000 species of orchids that include hybrids and 800 types native to Malaysia. These colorful plants thrive in abundance across this 2.5-acre (1- hectare) floral paradise.

Continue to the adjacent Kuala Lumpur Butterfly Park, where 80,000 square feet of landscaped gardens house more than 5,000 butterflies and butterfly-friendly vegetation. One of the world’s largest butterfly attractions, the park also features an information exhibit area and gift shop. Then visit the KL Bird Park, also within the Lake Gardens complex. Inside the 21-acre (8.5-hectare) aviary, marvel at more than 3,000 birds that represent more than 200 species; 10 percent are birds from overseas, while the rest are local species. Your last attraction is Aquaria KLCC, an oceanarium home to 5,000 aquatic creatures across a 60,000-square-foot space at the Kuala Lumpur Convention Centre. It’s one of the biggest aquariums in Southeast Asia. When you’ve absorbed as much nature and wildlife as you can, you’ll be dropped off at your hotel or another KL location, if you wish.

Chinatown, Kuala Lumpur is the oldest Chinese settlement in Kuala Lumpur. Divided by three parallel streets, Chinatown is well known for street food, daily wears and places of worship. Brick fields is the oldest Indian settlement in Kuala Lumpur and even though it is occupied by local Indians, Hinduism is not the only religion being practiced in this settlement. Ideal location for almost everything Indian.

Istana Negara (Gates of The Kings Palace), the official residence of the ruler of Malaysia.National Monument (War Memorial): A wonderful site to commemorate fallen heroes from the First World War, Second World War and the Emergency Period. Lovely area to drive or walk through to see the Butterfly Farm, Bird Park, Orchid Garden, Hibiscus Garden and many more interesting sites. Masjid Negara (National Mosque), officiated in1965, this mosque can accommodate fifteen thousand (15,000) worshipers at any one time. B. Hubback, this building is an architectural wonder of its time. This building and its surroundings will surely transport one back in time.
Independence Square(Merdeka Square) where Sultan Abdul Samad Building, Royal Selangor Club and St. Mary's Cathedral makes up the square.

You’ll also visit the National Mosque. Built in 1965, Masjid Negara is located in the very heart of the city amid lush green gardens. Admire one of the most elegant buildings in Kuala Lumpur, featuring a spectacular main dome covered in green and blue tiles, and the 48 smaller green domes spread across the Mecca-inspired courtyard. The Chinese Thean Hou Temple is beautiful synergy of styles as Buddhism, Taoism, and Confucianism join to form an unforgettable architectural ensemble. See numerous statues of animals from astrology and impressive statues of the Goddess of Mercy and the Goddess of the Waterfront.

See Lake Gardens, a beautiful and calming getaway from the bustle of the city. Visit the National Museum, home to collections of ancient and modern art pieces, weapons, and traditional costumes. Marvel at the exquisite façade of the Kuala Lumpur Railway Station, an ideal setting for a photo op, with its fairytale-like towers and mix of Eastern and Western architectural styles.

Also known as Tugu Negara, the National Monument commemorates the lives that were lost in the fight for Malaysian independence. Designed by Felix de Weldon, an American architect, this monument is the highest sculpture grouping made of bronze ever created. At the end of the tour you’ll be taken back to your hotel in a comfortable air-conditioned van.

You will depart on a long boat and enjoy some fishing activities (catch and release) before proceeding to the legendary Tasik Dayang Bunting (Pregnant Maiden Lake). Legend says that the water of the lake possesses some mystical power to help women bear children. This freshwater lake is cool and perfect for swimming, which you will be able to enjoy for approximately 40mins.

The boat will then take you to another Island where you will be able to witness birds of prey. There are a few different types of birds here but among the mostly commonly seen are the White-bellied Sea Eagle and the Brahminy Kite. Langkawi, the name of the island has been given after the reddish brown eagle. Helang in Malay means Eagle and Kawi is reddish brown color. The reddish brown eagles (also known as Brahminy Kites) are the most common form of eagles that you will find here. You will also see many White Bellied Sea Eagles in Langkawi as well which are larger in size.

The last island we will visit is Pulau Beras Basah (Wet Rice Island) a beautiful white sandy beach where it is possible to swim and enjoy a BBQ picnic. Pulau Beras Basah is famous for its beautiful white sandy beaches with crystal clear blue waters and the rich mystifying forest with magnificent mountains in the background. It an ideal place for you to get away for a while and indulge yourself in the beauty of nature. Besides its pristine white sand beaches, it offers other interesting activities too including (at own cost) Para sailing; snorkeling, banana boat ride swimming or you can just bathe and relax under the sun.

overview: On this 3-hour private tour of Pulau Langkawi (Langkawi Island), you’ll get acquainted with the cultural history and heritage of its inhabitants. expect: On this tour you will see traditional Malay housing on a visit to the Bon Ton Kampung Houses. We then move on to Mahsuri’s Tomb, Mahsuri is known to have been a very vengeful woman who cursed Langkawi for seven generations after she was wrongfully convicted and sentenced to death for adultery You will also check out whether the remains from the great battle between Garuda and Jentayu still exist (as some still believe), at Pantai Pasir Hitam Langkawi (Black Sand Beach in English). The peaceful Langkawi beach is stained with black sand - you'll find that not the whole beach is black but it's more like a mixture of black sand and normal sand. Unlike other black-sand beaches, this sand isn't volcanic in nature - iron oxide is believed to be the cause of this phenomenon.

Some people also believe that the black sand beach is caused by the the burnt soil from the rice fields that were burnt during the Siamese war. The burnt soil flowed to the sea got washed up on to this beach creating the black sand beach.

Just down the road, see the intricate and beautiful designs of Malaysian batik on display at a craft cultural center. Some people believe the waters of the lake possess mystical powers as a local princess has blessed the waters. Because of the blessings, it is believed that any woman who is unable to conceive may have a child after drinking the water from the lake.

Afterward, see the beautiful rural countryside of the island as you drive past quaint Malay villages, sprawling rice paddy fields with frolicking water buffaloes, and verant rubber plantations. overview: Discover the beauty of Langkawi Island on a half-day bike tour through the countryside. Stop by the Rice Garden Museum in Laman Padi during a moderate ride of 16 miles (26 km) with your guide.

Cycling along this beachside stretch, you’ll pass by souvenir stalls, bars and day spas. Soon you’ll escape the beach crowds and relish the tranquil surroundings of rustic villages flanked by rice fields. Take a break around Underwater World Langkawi to purchase a drink at a duty-free shop.

Further down the road is Laman Padi where you’ll gain entry to the Rice Garden Museum and its exhibits of equipment involved in rice cultivation, once Langkawi’s main industry. Pedal on country roads to a neighborhood kampong and receive a warm welcome by village residents. Stop for a tea break at a local home and learn about the history and culture of rural Langkawi from your guide.

Finally, you’ll come upon a rubber plantation and mangroves teeming with colorful birds, such as kingfishers and hornbills, as well as monitor lizards. On the return trip, bicycle through green pastures spreading as far as the eye can see. Hotel drop-off is included.

title.en: Langkawi Archipelago Jet Ski Tour Including Dayang Bunting Island

overview: Discover the delights of the Langkawi Archipelago on this 4-hour jet-ski tour. Hop onto your jet-ski and head onto the Andaman Sea with your guide. Enjoy breathtaking views over the crystal-blue seas and white sands of the Langkawi archipelago. Visit Dayang Bunting Island, widely considered the jewel in the archipelago’s crown. Admire forested hills and rocky outcrops, and hear of traditional island legends. Zoom among rocky outcrops and hidden bays on route to the Fjords, and enjoy personal attention from your guide on this small-group tour, limited to eight people.
highlights: Half-day Jet Ski tour of Langkawi archipelago
Ride solo or with a passenger on a convoy across turquoise waters to secret coves
Explore eight rocky islets with an experienced guide, including Dayang Bunting
Island

expect: Choose a morning or afternoon departure time, and meet your small group at a designated spot on Cenang Beach. After a safety briefing and instruction on how to operate your Jet Ski, hop aboard and follow an experienced guide who leads your convoy over the tranquil waters of the Andaman Sea to eight islands in the Langkawi archipelago. You can ride solo or double up with a partner, depending on the option you select upon booking. After a short stop at Tepur Island for a check-in and some advice from your guide on riding in formation, continue to the region’s second largest island and its star attraction: Dayang Bunting Island. Arrive at the lookout point for a glimpse of the pregnant maiden’s silhouette for which the island was named, formed by the outline of hills and rocky outcrops on one side of Dayang Bunting Lake — the largest freshwater lake in Malaysia. Hear about the legend of a lovely fairy princess who became pregnant after drinking the water, and then follow your guide on a 5-minute jungle trek to the lake, which is separated from the sea by a thin ridge of limestone. Enjoy free time to swim, or rent a solar boat or paddle boat. For those looking to unwind, just dip your feet in the water on a dock and enjoy the lush surroundings.

When it's time, get back on your Jet Ski and speed over to the Fjords, a cluster of jungle-clad islands about one nautical mile (2 km) away. Skim across the crystal-clear waters between rocky islets and secret coves to arrive at another dip-worthy spot where you'll be surrounded by 360-degree views of jungle terrain.

Catch the breathtaking sight of eagles soaring overhead while your guide describes the flora and fauna. A mushroom-shaped island, limestone structures, stalactites, mangroves, and other vegetation unique to Langkawi are among the geological and biological wonders you'll learn more about.
Before riding back to the starting point, stop at an uncharted island for a short swim and snorkeling session (depending on water conditions) to top off your half-day Jet Ski adventure.

expect: Gather with your small group at the meeting point on Cenang Beach in the morning or afternoon, depending on your selection upon booking. After a safety briefing and tips, you and your fellow experienced solo riders can hop on the Jet Skis to embark on a glorious 4- hour ride.

Race effortlessly along the Langkawi Island coastline, following your guide past the Awana Porto Malai, a marina where you can spot cruise ships and a holiday resort with unhindered ocean views. Rev your motor toward the Navy Pontoon for a glimpse of sturdy vessels, followed by the Langkawi Port, home to numerous wooden fishing boats and a giant eagle statue — a popular landmark on the pier.

Learn about Langkawi’s commerce and economy as you stop at Jetty Pelancongan in the town of Kuah, and the history of the Langkawi archipelago en route to the Royal Langkawi Yacht Club that features an array of luxury yachts.

You’ll head out to open waters, where dolphins sometimes race alongside the Jet Skis, for a ride to your final destination: Penarak fishing village. Discover Malay village life and culture as you follow your guide to a fisherman’s house that’s only accessible from the water, where you’re welcomed with a provided lunch including fried rice, fruit and tea. Enjoy a spectacular hilltop view over the turquoise waters of the Andaman Sea as you prepare for the greatest riding challenge of the day —a brisk ride to Monkey Beach for a brief dip in ocean waters before racing back to Cenang Beach, where your tour ends.

Then, we will embark on a boat for a river cruise to search for the endangered long nose monkeys of Borneo, the Proboscis Monkeys. You will see the Proboscis Monkeys in their own habitats, and get to see some other interesting mangrove inhabitants such as horn-bills, kingfishers and crocodile (if you are lucky). Enjoy scenes of village life as you watch children playing, fishermen returning home or buffaloes wallowing. expect: Travel for about 30 minutes away from the hustle and bustle of the city to the Inanam countryside for a visit to the Mari Mari Cultural village. Built to showcase the rich diversity of the people of Borneo, the village is set amidst secondary jungle providing an ideal setting to learn how each tribe has used materials commonly found in their surrounding environment in their everyday living.

To enter the village, you would have to cross a 20 meters hanging bridge spanning 13 feet (4 meters) above a flowing river. Enjoy a 90 minutes leisure walk as you visit the houses of the major tribal groups of Borneo namely the Dusun, Rungus, Lundayeh, Bajau and Murut Longhouse. overview: Explore the history and heritage of Sabah’s tribal inhabitants on this 4-hour Mari Mari Village cultural tour from Kota Kinabalu. Follow your guide through the Mari Mari Cultural Village and gain insight into the culture and traditions of Borneo’s indigenous groups. Learn of the diverse skills the tribespeople have come to rely on, such as fishing, rice-farming and hunting, and admire the traditional construction techniques in use deep in the jungle. expect: After pickup from your hotel, get comfortable in your shared minivan and head to Mari Mari Cultural Village, located deep in the rainforest about 25 minutes from central Kota Kinabalu. This village is like an open-air museum, dotted with various tribal dwellings and demonstration stations to give you insight into the history, traditions and lifestyle of Borneo's five main indigenous groups.

During your 4-hour tour, see how the island's inhabitants once lived as rice farmers (Kadazan- Dusun), longhouse residents (Rungus), hunters and fisherman (Lundayeh), cowboys and sea gypsies (Bajau), and the notoriously feared headhunters (Murut). Learn about traditional construction techniques as you observe megaliths, handcrafted buildings and a hanging bridge, and get a first-hand look at cultural customs such as fire starting, cooking and hunting. At the House of Skulls, find relics from Murut's headhunting days, including swords, costumes and even 42 ancient human skulls.

Enjoy a welcome drink of locally made rice wine before the highlight of your tour: an educational dance show and demonstration. In-house guides — who are descendants of the indigenous people — share stories about how their ancestors lived, and you can participate in a few of the rituals and traditions, including bamboo shooting! Depending on the tour time you select, you'll enjoy lunch, afternoon tea and snacks, or dinner before returning to your hotel.

expect: After you’re picked up early in the morning from your Kota Kinabalu city hotel, depart north by coach toward the Tip of Borneo, situated on the Kudat Peninsula. En route, stop in the town of Kota Belud where you can walk around and observe the locals conducting their daily activities as your guide offers insightful commentary on their lifestyle. Learn about the Bajau people, originally an indigenous seafaring group from the Philippines who now make their living as farmers and cattle ranchers, earning them the alias ‘cowboys of the east.’ Discover how these skilled horsemen are especially adept at sword making. On Sundays, a colorful and vibrant open-air market called Tamu is held. If you’re in town at this time, mingle amid the vendors selling local products, from foodstuffs to livestock and handicrafts.

Hop back aboard the coach and continue your journey further, with a stop at Kampung Gombizau to learn about the process of bee farming and honey harvesting. Visit a traditional Rungus longhouse and admire the unique structure made primarily of wood and bamboo. Hear your guide share information about the Rungus people, one of Sabah’s ethnic groups that still holds proudly to its cultural traditions, including elegantly crafted beadwork and ornamental items.

After a traditional lunch at the longhouse, your journey takes you to Tanjung Simpang Mengayau, aka the Tip of Borneo. Drive through a picturesque landscape until reaching the headland, and stand mesmerized by the captivating views of the South China Sea as you realize you’re at the northernmost edge of the world’s third largest island. Snap scenic photos and return to your coach, arriving back at your hotel in Kota Kinabalu in the late afternoon.
