Travel back in time to the days when locals journeyed by steam train to Sabah. You’ll relax on a refurbished train car that’s designed to evoke the sense of stepping into the 1900s, as you make your way on the 36-mile rail trip. Your trip begins at Tanjung Aru Station, where you’ll board the train and head out towards the pastoral landscapes of rural Malaysia. You’ll pass the coast of Lokawi Bay where window seat travelers have access to stunning views of the South China Sea. Make a visit to the traditional trading village of Kinarut, as well as Tien Shi Temple and enjoy a bit of free time to explore tiny shops in the foothills near the temple.

Your train ride continues through the Kawang Forest Reserve, over a steel bridge past the Papar River, finally ending in the town of Papar. Enjoy a taste of local life in the nearby wet market and engage with residents as you take in the sights, sounds and smells of this lively place. title.en: Manukan Island Day Trip from Kota Kinabalu

overview: Boomerang shaped Manukan is the second largest Island of the Tunku Abdul Rahman Park which has good stretches of beaches on the southern coastline. Manukan is the most beautiful, most visited and most recommended of the 5 islands. On this Island you can enjoy the sunlight, beautiful breaches, fun beach activities such as beach volleyball, parasailing and more! You can also enjoy snorkeling. The best site to snorkel is among the corals the darker color of the sea means there's a coral bed below the water. It is advised that you swim away from the boat pier and pillar. There is a 1500m track that extends throughout the island, eventually reaching the sunrise point. It is an absolutely stunning walk, and a must-do when visiting Manukan. The track can be quite steep at time, but it is fully paved the whole way. Please note: fishing is not allowed here as it can ruin the balance of the sea ecosystem.
highlights: Enjoy a day away from the hustle and bustle of the city
Family friendly

highlights: Cruise through the Klias Wetlands on the lookout for the elusive Proboscis monkeys and the rare Silver Leaf monkeys on this safari tour from Kota Kinabalu

title.en: 2-Day Pulau Tiga Island Tour from Kota Kinabalu

overview: Enjoy your very own ‘Survivor’-style adventure on this 2-day tour of Pulau Tiga island, the original filming site for the popular reality TV show. Get back to nature as you hike through the jungle, cruise to neighboring Snake Island and bathe in a mineral-rich mud volcano. Or why not make the most of your island adventure and add a canoeing, snorkeling or open-sea fishing excursion? This tour includes overnight accommodation, round-trip transfers from Kota Kinabalu and meals.
highlights: 2-day Pulau Tiga tour with overnight lodging and meals
Experience the healing properties of a mud volcano on Survivor Island
Go on a nature walk in search of megapodes and monitor lizards
Visit neighboring Snake Island for sightseeing, relaxation and optional activities (own expense) at the beach

Enjoy single or twin-share accommodations at Pulau Tiga Resort Relax on the 2-hour drive from Kota Kinabalu to Kuala Penyu, and ride a boat from the jetty to the island paradise Hotel pickup and drop-off included
expect: Located just 6 miles (10 km) off the coast of Sabah, Pulau Tiga is a great island getaway from Kota Kinabalu. A network of nature trails around ‘Survivor Island’ offers great hiking opportunities, and nearby Kalampunian Damit, aka Snake Island, is another fantastic place for swimming, snorkeling, fishing or boating around its clear turquoise waters. Enjoy basic overnight lodging at Pulau Tiga Resort, with single or twin-share accommodations including a private bathroom with hot shower, air-conditioning, ceiling fan, coffee/tea-making facilities, bottled drinking water and a balcony. Please note: A minimum of 2 people per booking is required.
Itinerary
Day 1: Kota Kinabalu – Pulau Tiga (L, D)

After hotel pickup in Kota Kinabalu by comfortable minivan, depart on a 2-hour drive to Kuala Penyu. From here, your guide accompanies you on a 30-minute boat ride to Pulau Tiga, aka Survivor Island, where you can check in at Pulau Tiga Resort. As you arrive at the jetty, be sure to peer into the crystal-clear water teeming with fish. Once you’re settled in at your accommodation, a buffet-style lunch is served at the restaurant located in the main building, but if weather permits you can enjoy your food at the Island Bar near the beach. Enjoy a dip in the turquoise waters or simply relax on the shore. In the afternoon, embark on a moderate, 20-minute guided walk along a nature trail to an area where you can bathe in the island’s famous volcanic mud; it's said to have therapeutic qualities for skin and hair.

Your guide shares geological formation of Pulau Tiga following the eruption of several mud volcanoes, island lore, or maybe even some tales about the popular TV series Survivor that was filmed here. Keep an eye out for numerous birds, mammals, amphibians and reptiles that find refuge here, including stocky, chicken-like birds called megapodes that are common to the island.
Your evening is free for you to spend at your leisure, and dinner is provided at the resort restaurant.
Overnight: Pulau Tiga Resort on Pulau Tiga
Day 2: Pulau Tiga – Snake Island – Kota Kinabalu (B, L)
Check out of your accommodation after a buffet-style breakfast at the resort. Then embark on an adventurous 20-minute speedboat ride to Snake Island, formally referred to as Pulau Kalampunian Damit.

During your short visit to the island enjoy great photo ops, and some sightseeing with your guide who shares information on marine life as well as flora and fauna. (Wonder how the island got its new name? It might have something to do with the hundreds of sea snakes that live here.) If you want to be more active, let your guide know. For an additional fee, you can canoe, snorkel, ride a boat around the island, or go fishing on the open sea, among other optional activities.
In the afternoon, proceed back to Kuala Penyu jetty and onward to Kota Kinabalu, where you’ll have lunch at a lodge restaurant before you’re dropped off at your next hotel.

highlights: 2-day small-group tour of Kinabalu National Park and Poring Hot Springs
Explore UNESCO World Heritage-listed Kinabalu National Park with your expert guide
Take in scenic views of the jungle's wildlife, waterfalls and streams as you stroll on the suspended canopy walkway

Day 1: Kota Kinabalu -- Kinabalu National Park (L, D)

After pickup from your hotel in Kota Kinabalu, you will be driven approximately two hours to Kinabalu National Park. Along the way, stop at a small market in Nabalu to peruse the folk handicrafts and fresh produce sold by local vendors.

Arrive at UNESCO World Heritage-listed Kinabalu National Park. Follow your guide on a 30-minute moderate uphill trek to get to the canopy wakway that spans a length of about 518 feet (158 m). Suspended about 134 feet (41 m) from the ground, its where you can take in incredible scenic views of the jungle’s waterfalls and wildlife. As you explore the jungle, discover why the park is considered one of the most important biological sites in the world. Then, soak away any aches you have in the pools at the Poring Hot Springs, which are alleged to have therapeutic properties from their sulphuric minerals. Board your transfer for a drive back to Kota Kinabalu in Sabah, where you will be dropped off at your own hotel.

title.en: 3-Day Mt Kinabalu Hiking Adventure from Kota Kinabalu

overview: Scale the mighty peak of Mount Kinabalu, a UNESCO World Heritage site and Malaysia’s highest mountain, on this challenging 3-day hike from Kota Kinabalu. Spend the first day exploring the Kinabalu National Park, then embark on a 7-mile (12km) round-trip hike to the mountaintop. Finally, watch the magnificent sunrise from the 13,451-foot (4,100-meter) summit of Low's Peak. This all-inclusive tour includes accommodation, meals and hotel transfers.
highlights: 3-day hiking adventure on Mt Kinabalu in Sabah
Experience UNESCO World Heritage-listed Mt Kinabalu, a very popular climbing spot
Follow your guide on two challenging yet rewarding hikes on the mountain and admire incredible views
Stay overnight at the Laban Rata rest house, nestled halfway up the mountain with gorgeous views
Watch a beautiful sunrise at Low’s Peak
No experience necessary!
All meals, accommodation and hotel transportation are included
expect: All meals, entrance fees and accommodation are included. You’ll hike approximately 7 miles (12 km) round-trip and your guide will always be available for assistance and support. There will be plenty of breaks along the way to rest, take in the scenery and refill your water bottles. Itinerary
Day 1: Kota Kinabalu -- Kinabalu National Park (L,D)

You’ll be picked up at your Kota Kinabalu hotel in the morning and taken to Kinabalu National Park. Follow your guide on a nature walk through the trails to learn about the park’s abundant flora and fauna. Or, if you prefer, have free time to explore the park on your own. Head to your hotel for check-in and then have lunch at a nearby restaurant. In the afternoon, visit the Mountain Garden with your guide to learn more about the park’s plant diversity. In the evening, enjoy another great meal at the same restaurant before heading back to your hotel.
Overnight: Kinabalu Park Hill Lodge/Liwagu Suite, Perkasa Hotel or Pine Resort in Kinabalu National Park
Day 2: Kinabalu National Park -- Mt Kinabalu (B,L,D)

Have breakfast at Balsam Restaurant, where you will also collect your boxed lunch of a sandwich, piece of chicken, fruit and water. Then, head to the park headquarters to meet your guide for a drive to Timpohon Gate.

When you arrive, receive a safety briefing and training on what to expect during your hike. Then, embark on a moderate 4-mile (6-km) hike with your guide. Depending on the group’s ability level, the hike will take between 6 and 8 hours.

Along a rainforest trail, you’ll see a beautiful waterfall. Stop at various huts along the way to rest and fill up your water bottle, and break for lunch in Layang Layang before continuing the second half of your hike, where you’ll enter a whole new landscape of forests, rocks and inclines.

Emerge onto a rocky plateau as you approach Laban Rata, a hotel on Mt Kinabalu. Upon check-in, freshen up for a buffet dinner at the dining hall at your desired time. Indulge in both Malaysian and Western dishes to refuel for your next day. Be sure to get to bed early, as tomorrow’s hike will be very early!
Overnight: Laban Rata on Mt Kinabalu
Day 3: Mt Kinabalu -- Kota Kinabalu (B, L)

Gear up for today’s hike around 2:30am. Follow your guide to the summit at Low’s Peak, a 2- mile (3-km) hike for a total of 3 or 4 hours. Navigate rock faces and take in views of the forest and valley during this exhilarating experience.
Your guide will be available for assistance and point out the best ways to approach tricky portions of the climb.

It’ll be around 6am when you reach the top of Low's Peak, giving you incredible views in all directions of St John's Peak to the west, Donkey's Ears to the east and the distinctive South Peak. You’ll be rewarded with a breathtaking sunrise at 13,451 feet (4,100 meters) – a truly unforgettable experience.

After enjoying the sunrise, return back to Laban Rata for a hearty breakfast and check-out. Make your way back down to Timpohon Gate on a 2- to 4-hour hike. Relax over lunch at Balsam Restaurant before being driven comfortably to your Kota Kinabalu hotel.

title.en: 3-Day Tour from Sabah: Sandakan Sightseeing and Wildlife Experience in Sepilok and Selingan

overview: Discover the beauty of Malaysia’s natural world on this 3-day Sandakan sightseeing and wildlife experience in Sepilok and Selingan from Sabah. Learn of the life cycle of green sea turtles on Selingan Turtle Island, and soak up the sunshine at your leisure. Trek through lowland rainforest to the Sepilok Orangutan Rehabilitation Centre. Take a boat safari along the Kinabatangan River and admire native wildlife along the riverbank. Explore the Gomantong cave system with your guide. Discover Sandakan attractions including Agnes Keith House and Sandakan Memorial Park during your city tour.
highlights: 3-day Sandakan city and wildlife experience from Sabah
Discover Malaysia’s lush natural scenery and wildlife with an expert local guide
See native animals up close on a Kinabatanga River boat safari and at two animal conservation facilities
Watch baby turtles scurry along the beach to the sea and see orangutans being fed in the rainforest
Journey inside a vast cave complex and enjoy several scenic boat rides
Take a Sandakan city tour and browse a bustling market full of local vendors
Transportation, meals and accommodation included
expect: Green sea turtles, forest orangutans and limestone caves are just some of the highlights on this extraordinary 3-day tour from Sabah to Sandakan, including 4-star overnight stays at Selingan Island Resort and Borneo Nature Lodge. All meals and transportation, including boat tours, are included as you're expertly guided to some of the region's best natural and cultural attractions.
Itinerary
Day 1: Sabah – Selingan Turtle Island (L, D)

Following pickup at your Kota Kinabalu hotel you’re taken to the airport for your flight to Sandakan (not included, please see Additional Info for details). Upon arrival, transfer to the jetty for a scenic 1-hour boat ride to Selingan Turtle Island, a major nesting area for green sea turtles.

After you check in to your hotel and have lunch, the rest of the afternoon is free for you to explore the island at your own leisure. Take a dip in the ocean, soak up the sun on the beach or discover marine life while snorkeling (own expense). The island offers a variety of fun activities — just ask your friendly guide.

After dinner, enjoy a unique nighttime experience as you listen to a park ranger explain how Selingan Island is a conservation area that protects turtles’ newly laid eggs from predators. If you’re lucky, you may witness workers collecting eggs from the nesting site and planting them in the hatchery, observe the awe-inspiring process of turtles eggs hatching, or see the magnificent sight of baby turtles scrambling on the beach to the open sea. Overnight: 4-star Selingan Island Resort on Selingan Island
Day 2: Selingan Turtle Island – Sandakan (B, L, D)

After breakfast, board a boat and travel along the Sulu Sea back to Sandakan, where you’ll be picked up for a short drive to the Sepilok Orangutan Rehabilitation Centre. Here, watch a video about the center’s important work of rehabilitating injured and orphaned orangutans. Then follow your guide on an easy trek along a wooden boardwalk through the lowland rainforest to a viewing platform to witness the feeding of orangutans. Next, enjoy on a scenic 2.5-hour drive through the rustic countryside studded with villages, and then take a short boat transfer to your hotel for check-in. You’ll have time to relax by the river before embarking on a 1.5-hour boat safari along the Kinabatangan River, Sabah's longest river. Travel through lush mangrove and rainforest habitats, spotting native wildlife along the way. Your guide will help point out a few primates such as proboscis monkeys as they settle onto treetops.
After your boat journey, return to the lodge for dinner.
Overnight: 4.5-star Borneo Nature Lodge in Sandakan
Day 3: Sandakan – Sabah (B, L)

After breakfast at the lodge, venture to Gomantong Cave, located in a large limestone outcrop, for an adventurous exploration of this massive cave complex famed for its edible birds' nests. Then walk for about 15 minutes along a boardwalk to the opening of Semut Hitam cavern and explore the cave system with your guide.

Return to Sandakan for lunch and then head on a city coach tour beginning with a visit to a bustling market to peruse its stalls offering fresh seafood and unique local delicacies. Visit historic sites like the Agnes Keith House, where the American author lived and where the British government was housed. Walk inside and see reproductions of colonial furniture and authentic antiques.

Next, visit Sandakan Memorial Park, commemorating the life of Australian and British prisoners of war during World War II. Tour the beautifully maintained park and the museum to learn about the heroic efforts of these POWs.
Afterward, you’ll be taken to the airport for your evening flight (not included) with a transfer back to your Kota Kinabalu hotel.

title.en: 2-Day Small-Group Tour: Sandakan City and Wildlife Experience from Sabah

overview: Explore the natural wonders and cultural heritage of Northern Borneo on this action-packed 2-day tour from Kota Kinabalu. Get up close to Borneo’s native orangutans at the Sepilok Orangutan Rehabilitation; spot turtles nesting and hatching on a night visit to Selingan Turtle Island; and enjoy swimming and snorkeling along the coast. Finally, visit landmarks like the Agnes Keith House and the Sandakan Memorial Park on a sightseeing tour of Sandakan. This small-group tour includes 4-star overnight accommodation, transfers and meals.
highlights: 2-day small-group tour of Sandakan and Selingan Turtle Island with an expert guide
Visit Selingan Turtle Island and learn about the important work of protecting of turtles and their offspring
Witness the incredible process of a turtle laying eggs!
Visit the Sepilok Orangutan Rehabilitation Centre and learn about the conservation and rehabilitation of injured and orphaned orangutans in Sandakan
Walk through the rainforest and watch the feeding of orangutans
Take a guided tour of Sandakan and visit historical sites such as the Agnes Keith House and Sandakan Memorial Park

expect: Discover the fascinating heritage of Sandakan and its neighboring island of Selingan on this all-inclusive 2-day small-group tour with your expert guide. Venture to Selingan, commonly referred to as Selingan Turtle Island, to observe the process of protecting baby turtles. Then, visit the Sepilok Orangutan Rehabilitation Centre to learn about the rehabilitation of stray and wounded orangutans.
Itinerary
Day 1: Sabah – Selingan Turtle Island (L, D)

To begin your 2-day tour, you will be picked up by your guide from your Kota Kinabalu hotel in Sabah and taken to the airport for your flight to Sandakan (flight not included, please see Additional Information for more details). Upon arrival, transfer to the Sandakan jetty for a 1- hour scenic boat ride to Selingan Turtle Island, where you’ll head to the hotel for check-in and lunch. Spend the rest of the afternoon exploring the island at your own leisure and expense. Take a dip in the ocean; soak up the sun on the beach; or discover marine life while snorkeling – the island offers a variety of fun recreational activities for you to enjoy. After dinner, enjoy an exciting and unique nighttime experience -- watching green turtles lay eggs on the beach! The island is a conservation area that protects turtles’ newly laid eggs from predators by transplanting them to the hatchery and then releasing baby turtles to the sea once they have hatched. With your expert guide, watch a turtle laying eggs; see the process of transplanting the eggs; and witness baby turtles being released to the open sea! Overnight: Selingan Island Resort on Selingan Island
Day 2: Selingan Turtle Island – Sandakan – Sabah (B, L)

After breakfast, board a boat that will take you along the Sulu Sea back to Sandakan. You’ll be picked up for a drive 15 miles (25 km) to the Sepilok Orangutan Rehabilitation Centre. Here, watch a video to learn about the center’s important work of rehabilitating injured and orphaned orangutans. Then, follow your guide on a 10-minute trek along wooden plank walkways through the rainforest to witness the feeding of orangutans. Head back to Sandakan for lunch with your fellow travelers at a popular restaurant chosen by your guide before spending the rest of the day on a guided city tour by comfortable vehicle. Stop at a bustling city market to peruse its many stalls that offer a variety of fresh seafood and unique local delicacies. Then, visit historically significant places like the Agnes Keith House, a restored building where well-known American author Agnes Keith and her family once lived and housed the British colonial government. Walk around inside the house and see reproductions of colonial furniture and authentic antiques, as well as a timeline of the Keith family.

Make your way to the Sandakan Memorial Park, a site commemorating the life of many Australian and British prisoners of war during World War 2. Take a guided tour of the beautifully maintained park and the museum, where you can learn more about the heroic efforts of these POWs.
After touring Sandakan, transfer to airport for the late afternoon flight (not included) back to your Kota Kinabalu hotel.

title.en: Full-Day Sepilok Orangutan and Sun Bear and Sandakan City Trail

overview: Meet gentle, shy orangutans in their natural habitat at a unique wildlife sanctuary on this delightful full-day tour. The Orangutan Rehabilitation Center in Sandakan is located in the middle of the lush Sepilok Forest Reserve. The Center specializes in caring for baby orphan orangutans and teaching them the survival skills they would have learned from their mothers under normal conditions. The orangutans are not kept in captivity but rather come and go as they please while becoming used to living in the wild again after being held in captivity by various people. You will have the chance to see these incredible creatures close up and to watch the fun of feeding time.

Visit the Nature Education Center and watch the video documentary show to learn about the rehabilitation of orphaned Orangutan before taking a boardwalk through the lowland rainforest to view the feeding platform. Trek ten minutes through the rainforest on wooden plank walks to witness the feeding of the Orangutans at approximately 10am.

After this, you will be transferred to the Bornean Sun Bear Conservation Center, where you will see the Sun Bear live in tropical regions with year-round available foods. During time of mating, the Sun Bear will show behavior like hugging, mock fighting and head bobbing with its mate.
Enjoy a delicious lunch before proceeding to the Sandakan City Tour. You will be shown various landmarks and historical points in the city that was once known as “Little Hong Kong”.

Landmarks you will see include Puh Jih Syh Buddhist Temple which offers a panoramic view of Sandakan Bay situated on the hill top Tanah Merah and Sandakan Central Market which has the most amazing variety of fresh seafood and agricultural products. You will also take a visit to the English Tea House – a display of traditional British colonial architecture and uniform. The English tea house has a typically British menu including such favorites as fish and chips, shepherd's pie and cream teas. The concept of a colonial style English restaurant was an idea inspired by the famous Agnes Keith house next door. Contact Nobles Tours for recommended flights.

When you reach Gaya, embark on 1.5-hour hike through the dense tropical jungle. Trek along a 1-mile (1.6-km) trail with your guide, gazing up at 100-foot-tall (30-meter) trees, listening for the trill of hornbills, and looking for native flora, fauna and wildlife. Ratan plants, bamboo trees and wild mushrooms frame the footpath as lizards scamper by. After your hike, gear up for an exciting zipline ride! Receive a safety briefing, put on your equipment and take off across 820 feet (250 meters) of zipline cable, soaring at blazing speeds of up to 40 mph (65 kph). Soak up aerial views of Tunku Abdul Rahman National Park and cross the calm 328-foot (100-meter) channel dividing the Gaya and Sapi islands, looking down on cerulean waters dotted by forested isles.

Zip down to a safe landing on Sapi and have free time to relax, soak up the scenery and purchase lunch in town on your own. At the end of your eco-adventure, board the boat and cruise back to the mainland, where you'll be transferred by private minivan back to your hotel.

title.en: Full-Day Kinabalu Park and Poring Hot Spring

overview: This park is a UNESCO World Heritage site with incredible mega bio-diversity of flora and fauna, a heaven for nature enthusiasts. On arrival, enjoy a guided nature trek along one of the many trails in the park before proceeding to the beautiful Poring Hot Springs which offers visitors the opportunity for an invigorating dip into its hot sulfur springs. For a closer look at nature, take the 41m high canopy walk which offers a spectacular view of the Borneo Rainforest flora and fauna.
highlights: Enjoy fantastic aerial views
Family friendly
Lunch included
expect: Your day will begin with a pickup form your hotel lobby. You will then be taken to the UNESCO World Heritage Site Kinabalu Park. The journey will take about 1.5 hours, however it is sure to speed by as you enjoy the views of the passing villages and paddy fields along mountainous roads that wind along the Crocker Range. There will also be a brief stop along the way at Nabalu. Nabalu is a place where the local natives gather to sell local produce, home grown fruit and vegetables and handicraft souvenirs.

Upon arrival at Kinabalu Park, you will notice the change in air temperature. Enjoy the refreshing and cooling air as you proceed for a walk along the nature trails in the Botanical garden. If the day is clear, you may even have the majestic experience of spotting Mount Kinabalu.

After lunch, depart for another interesting wonder, the Poring Hot Spring. Approximately 47km from Kinabalu Park, Poring Hot Spring got its name from the tall bamboo plant that is abundant in that area. At this natural hot spring, there are Japanese baths where you can soak yourself and let the invigorating water stimulate your body. It is believed to have curative powers.

You can also try the Treetop Canopy Walk, where bridges are suspended at the top of the tropical jungle creating a thrilling and inspiring experience. Feel like you’re flying as you stand 41m above ground level. A 20 minute hike is required to reach the Canopy Walk. After the tour is complete you will be taken back to your hotel.

title.en: The Coral Flyer Zipline Adventure at Tunku Abdul Rahman Park from Kota Kinabalu

overview: Book this trip to Tunku Abdul Rahman Park and experience the Coral flyer zip-line activity from Kota Kinabalu. It is the world’s largest island-to-island zip-line at 820 feet (250 meters) long from Gaya Island to Sapi Island. Enjoy wind blowing on your face and the excitement of zipping over the crystal clear waters.
highlights: Enjoy fantastic aerial views
All entrance fees included
Lunch included
Travel by boat and see the sights from the water
Family friendly
Enjoy a day away from the hustle and bustle of the city
expect: You will be picked up from your hotel lobby early in the morning and heading to the Jessleton Point Jetty for the zipline activity. The Coral Flyer Zipline will serve you with beautiful views, with the breeze caressing your face and the thrill of zipping over the sparkling clear waters of the TAR (Tunku Abdul Rahman) marine park.

Upon arrival, you will be transported to Gaya Island (where the zipline starts). All the safety equipment such as harnesses and helmets will be provided and you need to take hike to get the top of the island where the zipline is, an amazing view as soon as you get on the top. The water is sparkling blue, the Sapi Island beach in the distance is glowing, and the whole scene is framed by the leaves of Gaya Island’s tall trees.

You will be sent off down the zipline to Gaya Island after a short safety briefing. Each ride can accommodate two persons at one time and the extreme experience takes a total of about 25-30 seconds, the speed of the ride differs for every single person. For those with bags and equipment, fear not as they have a transfer service for your bags where they bring it over to your end point.

After the ride, you dismount at the end of the zipline at a station on Sapi Island. You are allowed to get off and take some photos with the incredible scene behind you, and then you'll have to take another short hike down to the Sapi Island beach area. You will be transported back to hotel safely after this incredible experience!

title.en: PADI Scuba Diving in Tunku Abdul Rahman Marine Park from Kota Kinabalu

overview: Enjoy an introduction to scuba diving on this 6-hour PADI course in Tunku Abdul Rahman Marine Park from Kota Kinabalu. Cruise into the Tunku Abdul Rahman National Park and admire panoramic views over the islands of Pulau Manukan and Pulau Gaya. Listen to step-by-step instructions from your guide and learn how to use your equipment. Then, descend beneath the waves on two dives and marvel at the coral seascape below. Watch colorful puffer fish and stingrays swimming through the crystal-clear waters, and watch the waves for graceful sea turtles.
highlights: PADI 'discover scuba diving' experience from Kota Kinabalu
Make the most of an experience aimed at non-certified and newly qualified divers
Cruise by speedboat to Tunku Abdul Rahman National Park (TARP)
Learn basic scuba diving skills in shallow water and make a beach entry for a first dive
Enjoy a second dive from the boat, and spot macro marine life and schools of clownfish among soft and hard corals
Receive individualized attention with a maximum of four beginning divers per PADI- certified instructor
Includes all diving equipment plus round-trip transport from selected hotels
expect: After a hotel pickup from Kota Kinabalu, travel to the Jesselton Point ferry terminal. From here, it’s about a 20-minute speedboat ride to Tunku Abdul Rahman National Park (TARP), home to the five pristine protected islands of Pulau Manukan, Pulau Gaya, Pulau Sapi, Pulau Mamutik and Pulau Sulug.

It's also where you'll discover some of the world’s best scuba diving, especially for beginners. Before making two dives, receive a step-by-step introduction to scuba diving, and learn how to suit up and use your diving equipment from your PADI-certified instructor. No prior experience is necessary and you can expect to receive personalized attention. Each instructor only works with a total of four divers at any given time. If you are more advanced and want to join, no problem! No challenging diving takes place during the experience, but divers of all abilities are sure to find the park stunning to explore.

After a briefing, follow your dive guide into chest-high water in the ocean to learn emergency procedures and basic scuba diving skills such as how to breathe, equalize the air spaces in your body, and clear your mask.

Following an overview of the skills you’ve learned, it’s time for the first dive. Enter from the beach to swim out to a training reef no deeper than 39 feet (12 meters). There is less coral but plenty of amazing fish to see during this practice session, which lasts 30-45 minutes. And don't fret about being in unfamiliar waters — your instructor remains close at all times. Back on shore, hop aboard the speedboat for a ride to one of the islands where you can purchase lunch and rest. (Bottled water is provided on the boat.) After lunch, take your afternoon dive from the boat, descending to a maximum depth of 39 feet (12 meters). Over the course of this 45-minute dive, with little or no current, take in the topography of the site — reef made of soft and hard corals where nudibranchs, pufferfish, lionfish, stingrays, sea stars, cuttlefish and moray eels are among the macro marine life you might see. Search for schools of barracuda and snapper, all seven species of clownfish, and sea turtles as you kick around the underwater paradise.
Once you’ve completed both dives, you’re returned to the jetty and dropped off at your selected hotel in the afternoon.

title.en: Half-Day Mari Mari Cultural Village from Kota Kinabalu

overview: Visit the Mari Mari Cultural Village, an open-air museum that introduces you to Borneo’s ethnic cultures. Visit longhouses in the village and observe the daily routines of Sabah’s traditional groups including the Dusun, Rungus, Lundayeh, Bajau and Murut. Taste Sabahan specialties for lunch and witness cultural demonstrations such as blowpipe making, fire starting and tattooing while you learn from your guide about the mystical symbolism behind these practices. Round-trip transport from Kota Kinabalu hotels included.
highlights: Mari Mari Cultural Village tour
Learn about the Dusun, Rungus, Lundayeh, Bajau and Murut cultures
See blowpipe making and fire starting demonstrations
Take in the delicious smell of bamboo cooking before lunch
Hotel pickup and drop-off included from Kota Kinabalu
expect: Your day will begin with a hotel pickup. Upon arrival at your first destination, you will be greeted and as preparation for your time-traveling adventure into prehistoric Borneo, briefing on the Village Rules is a must before you enter. You will be greeted by the Chief and together go through a village custom welcome ceremony. You will then walk over a suspended bridge to enter the village.

Once inside, you will visit the Dusun House. Here, you will witness a demonstration on the traditional way of tobacco cutting. As you exit through the back door, you will enter a hut specialized for bamboo cooking and Montoku (rice wine) processing. Next, we will bring you to the Rungus Longhouse. Here, you will learn how to start a fire without lighters or matches (and watch the villagers make ethnic bangles out of rattan). After this you will be taken to the Lundayeh house. Inside, be awed by a demonstration on the olden ways of producing ropes, vests, floors, walls and etc. from tree barks. Your fourth destination will be the Bajau House to watch the locals prepare Jala (local cake) and Pandan juice. Inside, you will see a myriad of colorful materials of antique ancestral objects. At one corner, there is a decorative bridal parlor for your photo-taking pleasure. After this you will visit the Murut Longhouse, belonging to the head-hunter’s tribe, you will be greeted by the Chief and go through a custom Welcome Ceremony. Later, witness a demonstration on blowpipe making before going into their house. Inside, there is a built-in Lansaran (traditional trampoline-like floor) which you may dance on after they show you how to jump for your prize. At a corner, witness the locals as they tattoo their bodies the old method. You can also get a temporary body tattoo the ancient way if you wish. Finally, you will be led to the stage where our very own staff will entertain you with cultural performances. After that, proceed to the main hall where you will be given fifteen minutes to linger around and shop at the Souvenir shop (all handmade products). You may also choose to take photos of your surroundings.

After your wonderful tour, a delicious meal will be prepared for you at the Buffet counter. Then, it is time to bid farewell to the villagers and depart into the 21st century, as we transfer you to your respective hotels/drop-off points.

title.en: Countryside Dinner with Panoramic View in Kota Kinabalu

overview: Enjoy a panoramic tour of Kota Kinabalu countryside as you traverse up Kokol hills to 2625 feet (800 meters) elevation. Stop for a spectacular view of the city and surrounding suburbs. Enjoy the serenity of village life as you pass by a typical Dusun community. On a clear day you can enjoy a magnificent view of Mount Kinabalu soaring above the Crocker Range. Complete your rustic experience with a typical Malaysian Hot Pot dinner at a hilltop restaurant where on a nice day, you may view an amazing sunset before the city awakens at night in full panoramic view.
highlights: See the sights illuminated at night
Enjoy a romantic night including dinner
Enjoy fantastic aerial views
Dinner included
Family friendly
Enjoy a day away from the hustle and bustle of the city
expect: Meet at the main hotel lobby around 4pm as you escape from the city life to the suburbs of Menggatal. Veer off the main road through countryside roads for about 30 minutes as you ascend to 2625 feet (800 meters) above sea level for a panoramic view of the Kota Kinabalu suburbs. En-route catch a glimpse of a typical Dusun village where you may be able to see buffaloes grazing by the roadside and village children playing football in the village field. On the other side of the Kokol mountain range, on a clear day, Mount Kinabalu can be seen towering above the longest range in Sabah - the Crocker Range. The menu for the Countryside Dinner is a Hot Pot Dinner, which is another typical Malaysian cuisine. Locally known as Steamboat, this form of dinner is usually encouraged among families and friend to create interaction and fun while cooking and eating together. A pot of soup is placed on top of a gas cooker. When boiled, a wide variety of raw ingredients are intermittently cooked and consumed as the dinner progresses. With the temperature at Kokol usually below 24C, having a freshly cooked hot dinner becomes a welcoming experience. The soup, in addition, becomes tastier each minute from the flavors of the seafood and meat which acts as a base for the finale which is normally the noodles.
For those who do not wish to cook their own dinner, set dinner or vegetarian set is available but we wish to advise that due the cold weather, the food do get cold very fast.

expect: The PADI Open Water Course in Kota Kinabalu diving on the islands in the Tunku Abdul Rahman Park which consist of Gaya, Sapi, Manukan, Mamutik and Sulug. This will enables you to, dive to a depth no greater than 60 ft (18m) independently with a certified buddy that has the equivalent or higher level certification while applying the knowledge and skills that you learned during the PADI Diving course.

You will be able to plan your dive and dive your plan, log open water no stop (no decompression) dives and discover the underwater world and forever blow bubbles in the Tunku Abdul Rahman Park by continuing on and taking the PADI advanced diver course package or taking the daily fun diving package in Kota Kinabalu. In the confined water dives you will apply dive principles, learn and practice Dive Safety procedures and skills. You’ll do this in confined water in a controlled environment inside the Tunku Abdul Rahman Park. Knowledge development gives you the information that you’ll need to complete your open water final exam. You will complete knowledge reviews, diver quizzes, and learn how to calculate your scuba dives by using the recreational dive planner. In the open water dives, you will apply what you have learned during confined open water and knowledge development and discover the underwater world at its best. You will complete four open water dives. This certification shows that you successfully completed the course according to the WRSTC (World Recreational Scuba Training Council), and dive centers or resorts would require this as a proof of certification.

Our PADI diving instructors teach in small groups (4:1) in Kota Kinabalu's marine park. title.en: 2-Tank Dive in Tunku Abdul Rahman Park

overview: Explore beautiful dive spots off the coast of Sabah on this 6-hour scuba-diving experience in Tunku Abdul Rahman Park from Kota Kinabalu. Hop aboard your speedboat with your guide and zoom into the Tunku Abdul Rahman National Park, home to dive sites suited to certified divers of all levels. Visit two dive sites around Manukan Island and enjoy 45-minute dives with your guide at each one. Search the coral for colorful sea life including clownfish and snapper, and keep your eyes open for graceful stingrays, turtles and blue-spotted octopus.
highlights: 2-tank scuba diving tour at Tunku Abdul Rahman Park (TARP)
Ride a speedboat through the marine park to Manukan Island, where you can purchase lunch

expect: After pickup from selected hotels in Kota Kinabalu, hop into a speedboat with your crew, dive guides and provided gear. Only 15 minutes by boat from Sabah, the Tunku Abdul Rahman National Park (TARP) offers plenty of dive sites suitable for certified beginner to experienced divers.

Speed away to Manukan Island, aka Pulau Manukan, one of five idyllic isles in TARP including Gaya, Sapi, Mamutik and Sulug. Lunch can be purchased at Jesselton Point before departure. Alternatively, local stores on Manuka Island sell sandwiches and fried rice plates. Bottled water is provided.

You'll visit two dive sites for a maximum of 45 minutes each, with one hour on the surface in between each dive. Average depth ranges from 16–33 feet (5–10 meters); maximum diving depth is 59 feet (18 meters), with good visibility between 33–49 feet (10–15 meters). Expect little or no current.

Follow your divemaster into the water and search for schools of barracuda and snapper, plus all seven species of clownfish that swim among the soft and hard corals. Macro marine life is most common in these waters, such as nudibranchs, pufferfish, lionfish, stingrays, starfish, cuttlefish and moray eels. There are plenty of larger animals, too: stingrays, hawksbill or green turtles, and the occasional blue-spotted octopus.
Once you’ve completed the dives, you’re taken back to shore and dropped off at your selected hotel.

Paddle your way past roaring rapids, then take a break during the calmer stretches for body rafting and swimming in the refreshing waters. Finish your trip with a tasty BBQ meal for lunch. expect: Take a refreshing plunge down the Grade II and III white water near Kota Kinabalu on this 6- hour rafting trip. Everyone from novices to river-rafting pros will enjoy this fun-filled ride set amongst the beautiful natural environment of Sabah's Kiulu River. Start your rafting journey with pickups from your Kota Kinabalu, Rasa Ria or Nexus area hotel around 9:45am. Please confirm the exact time with Nobles Tours, as your pickup may occur earlier. Then sit back for a picturesque 1-hour drive, passing through the rural city of Tamparuli on your way to the hilly region of Kiulu. The trip takes place along a sealed road, which finishes its last stretch on a village track that traverses the area's hilly terrain. Once you arrive at your put-in site along the Kiulu River, listen to an introduction to the techniques of river rafting. Then climb aboard your vessel and shove off for a thrilling ride. Your bamboo-shaded river path, and cool rushing water, offers the perfect sanctuary from the area's intense heat. Soon you hit the waterway's Grade II and III rapids, paddling hard to pass through these exhilarating stretches, after which you'll have a moment to relax in the calmer sections with some body rafting and swimming.
Upon completing 1 to 1.5 hours of rafting, top off your trip with a delicious BBQ meal, followed by drop-off back at your hotel.

Your boat then roams the mangrove-lined rivers looking for wildlife. As the light starts to fade we go in search of the rare proboscis monkey. Small groups are often seen in the treetops at the water edge, settling down for the night. As dusk arrives we search for fireflies and crocodiles. Crocodiles are often seen on the mud banks and brightly shining crocodile eyes can be spotted when a torch light is passed over the river.

After searching for crocodiles your boat proceeds further up river where fireflies gather at night. Watch the fireflies move around the branches of the mangroves, momentarily lighting up the night sky. After enjoying a firefly light show you return to the boat club and our driver will transfer you back to your hotel safely.

title.en: 2-Day Private Tour from Kuching: Cultural Experience in Serubah Village

overview: Experience the unique culture and traditions of Sarawak’s indigenous people with this immersive 2-day tour from Kuching, including accommodation and meals. Accompanied by a private guide, you’ll cruise along the Lemanak River by longboat, visit an authentic Serubah longhouse and tuck into typical Iban cuisine. This is a unique opportunity to learn about indigenous Iban culture as you chat with locals, browse local markets, try hunting with blowpipes and enjoy traditional dance, music and games.
highlights: 2-day tour to the Sarawak village of Serubah with a private guide
Tour the inside of a Serubah longhouse and discover indigenous Iban culture and heritage
Experience the friendly nature of the Iban community as you partake in evening entertainment like dancing and games
Learn about the Iban's way of tracking and hunting

Cruise along the Lemanak River on a traditional longboat

expect: Day 1: Kuching – Serubah (L,D) After pickup from your Kuching hotel in a private, air-conditioned minivan or bus, relax on the three-hour drive through the lush green countryside and enjoy scenic views of paddy fields and rugged, jungle-clad mountains.

Along the way, stop at a native farmers’ market in the town of Serian that offers a variety of jungle produce, including the fruit that Serian is famous for – durians! Follow your guide on a tour of a typical black pepper garden, where you will also see carnivorous pitcher plants. Enjoy lunch at a small roadside bazaar before continuing your journey. Arrive at the Lemanak River jetty in mid-afternoon. Admire views of the jungle on either side of the Lemanak River as you travel by longboat to the village of Serubah, where the locals – the indigenous Iban people – live in traditional Borneo longhouses. With the help of your guide, learn about the daily Iban lifestyle and see how some longhouses are equipped with modern facilities like electricity and water supply.

Sit down for a traditional Iban dinner, made with fresh produce, and then take part in an after- dinner cultural experience: an evening filled with traditional dancing, music, games and a glass or two of tuak (rice wine) with the longhouse chief. When you’ve had enough fun, retire for the night in your guesthouse, where you will truly gain your authentic experience of how village locals live. Sleep in your dormitory-style accommodation (one room for your private group) on a mattress placed on the floor, surrounded by a mosquito net. Overnight: Traditional guesthouse with modern facilities in Serubah village Day 2: Serubah – Kuching (B, L) After breakfast, discover more of the Iban heritage as you watch a blowpipe demonstration; the Iban use these instruments to hunt wild animals. You can even try shooting one yourself! Then, follow your guide and Iban trackers on a short walk through the forest, learning about the traditional uses of rainforest plants.
Bid farewell to your new friends and re-board the longboat for the return trip to the Lemanak jetty. Then drive back to Kuching, stopping for lunch along the way at a popular Sarawak restaurant.

expect: This award-winning living museum showcases Sarawak's unique and diverse cultures in an accessible, visitor-friendly setting just 35 minutes drive from Kuching. The seven authentic traditional buildings are set amidst a scenic 17 acre site and are populated by members of Sarawak's many ethnic groups, going about everyday activities. These include wood and bamboo carving, bead work, weaving, sago-making, sugar-cane crushing, pepper- growing and the preparation of bird's nests.

Visitors can learn how to throw a Malay spinning top, shoot a Penan blowpipe or pick out a tune on an Orang Ulu sape. The tour concludes with a colourful multi-ethnic cultural performance in the village's air-conditioned mini-theater.

overview: Discover Sarawak’s culture, history and natural beauty on this private 2-day Kuching sightseeing tour from Kuching. Explore Kuching with your private guide and admire top attractions including Tua Pek Kong Temple, St Joseph Cathedral, the Syariah Court, Satok Market and the Astana. expect: Day 1: Kuching — Semenggoh — Annah Rais (D) Meet your private guide upon pickup from your hotel or Kuching International Airport and proceed by minivan to the Semenggoh Wildlife Centre. Drive for 30 minutes until you reach the gateway to the lush tropical forest — inaccessible by car — where you’ll hop out and walk 20 minutes for the final mile.

Established in 1975 to care for injured, orphaned or illegally captured wildlife, the center occupies 1,828 acres (740 hectares) of unspoiled forest in the Semenggoh Nature Reserve and is the only one of its kind in Sarawak. Observe orangutans, bears, hornbills, porcupines, storks, eagles, deer and monkeys that were rescued from captivity, rehabilitated and raised in their natural surroundings to be released later back into wild, and gain insight into the center’s rehabilitation program from your guide.

Afterward, head to Kuching for a unique city tour aboard a surrey — a carriage-style bike with four wheels and a shade cover. On your 2.5-hour tour, see the gigantic cat statues near Jalan Padungan, cruise through Chinatown to Tua Pek Kong Temple, stop at a mosque along the Sarawak River, and see St Joseph Cathedral, the Syariah Court, Satok Market, the old courthouse and traditional Malay houses built on stilts. Across the Sarawak River, view the majestic Astana, a former palace of the second White Rajah. End with a tour of the Sarawak Museum, one of Maylasia’s oldest museums, displaying interesting archaeological and cultural artifacts.

Have lunch at a restaurant recommended by your guide (own expense) before leaving Kuching behind for Annah Rais, a 1-hour drive away. Arrive at the Bidayuh Longhouse, a village in an isolated valley home to around 120 local families. Take a private tour to learn about the history of the village and the life of its inhabitants, and learn how its strategic location kept the villagers safe from Borneo's notorious Murut headhunters. Your host family will prepare a simple, traditional dinner for you to enjoy while learning about their culture, beliefs and customs.

overnight: Longhouse homestay in Annah Rais Day 2: Annah Rais — Kuching (B) Wake up to a home-cooked breakfast prepared by your host family. Then ride your private minivan back to Kuching to conclude your tour. You’ll be dropped off at your hotel or the airport for your onward flight.

title.en: Turtle Watching at Night in Cherating

overview: Be mesmerized by the sight of sea turtles lumbering slowly up the white sandy beaches of Cherating to lay eggs. Known to swim great distances, these gentle creatures have chosen beaches near Cherating to come ashore in droves to lay eggs. This is an amazing experience that can be experienced only from May to September, so don't miss it!
highlights: Popular choice with kids

expect: Experience a yearly affair of the sea-faring turtle’s return on the beaches to lay their eggs with us. These nesting grounds are monitored by the Malaysian Fishery Department with rules and regulations, and best periods witness this is from May to September, especially during the high tide. We'll try our best to find turtles, but nature works on its own terms and there is no guarantee of turtle sightings.

Green turtles may grow over one meter in carapace length and weigh between 308-573 pound (140 - 260 kg). The green turtle is usually olive-brown in color, it is named for the color of its fat. The English name is Green Turtle, the scientific one is Chelonia mydas and the Malay Name is Penyu Agar.
Habitat and Ecology of Green Turtles :

They are almost exclusively vegetarian and feed on algae, sea grasses and sometimes on sponge. In Malaysia, green turtles nest on sandy beaches of the coast and offshore islands of Peninsular Malaysia, Sabah and Sarawak.
